early.criticalSuccess: Some farmhands wanted training with spears to better protect the village. They turned up on the green with borrowed spears and sore backs from the harvest, and by sundown they were marching in step and talking about the realm as theirs to defend.
early.success: Some farmhands wanted training with spears to better protect the village. They gathered on the green once the last sheaves were in. Nobody will mistake them for knights, but they know which end of the spear goes forward now.
early.failure: Some farmhands wanted training with spears to better protect the village. They came to the green, but with the harvest dragging on, half drifted home before noon and the drills fizzled out before anyone learned much.
early.criticalFailure: Some farmhands wanted training with spears to better protect the village. What began as spear drill on the green turned into a shoving match between two farms' boys, someone took a shaft to the head, and the whole thing broke up in angry words.

middle.criticalSuccess: Captains from three villages wanted to train their militias together before the roads dried. The three met on the muddy fields, and by the end of the week the captains were trading men and shouting the same calls. Their militias move as one now.
middle.success: Captains from three villages wanted to train their militias together before the roads dried. They worked their men hard through the spring rain, and while they're rough at the edges, the three militias can hold a line side by side.
middle.failure: Captains from three villages wanted to train their militias together before the roads dried. They met as planned, but each insisted on his own drills and his own calls, and the men went home no better than they came and a little more suspicious of each other.
middle.criticalFailure: Captains from three villages wanted to train their militias together before the roads dried. The joint training fell apart over who would command, two captains came to blows in front of their men, and the villages are sulking at one another.

late.criticalSuccess: Every banner in the realm wanted to march past the capital on the same day, which could have been glorious or chaos. It was glorious: they marched past on a bright morning in perfect order, crowds lined the road for miles, and foreign visitors went home talking about it.
late.success: Every banner in the realm wanted to march past the capital on the same day. There were a few tangles at the bridges, but the banners passed in good order and the crowds cheered every one.
late.failure: Every banner in the realm wanted to march past the capital on the same day, and too many tried to cross the same bridge at once. The Grand Muster turned into a long, muddy wait, and most of the crowd went home before the end.
late.criticalFailure: Every banner in the realm wanted to march past the capital on the same day, and it was chaos: two companies clashed over their place in the line, horses bolted into the crowd, and the realm was a laughingstock for a season.

early.criticalSuccess: A ford on the Sellen had no lookout, and smugglers had noticed. A lookout went up within days, and on the very first night the watch caught a smuggler's raft halfway across. Word spread fast that the ford is watched now.
early.success: A ford on the Sellen had no lookout, and smugglers had noticed. A watchman was posted, and the smugglers who'd grown used to the easy crossing found it watched and took their trade elsewhere.
early.failure: A ford on the Sellen had no lookout, and smugglers had noticed. A watchman was found, but he slept more than he watched, and the smugglers learned his habits within the week.
early.criticalFailure: A ford on the Sellen had no lookout, and smugglers had noticed. The man set to watch it was in the smugglers' pay from the start, goods are flowing over the river faster than ever, and folks are angry it took this long to notice.

middle.criticalSuccess: A border beacon manned by the realm's own people had gone unlit for a week. It turned out to be a forgotten duty that slipped between two villages, a proper roster went up along the whole border, and every beacon has burned since.
middle.success: A border beacon manned by the realm's own people had gone unlit for a week. Someone finally worked out whose job it was, it burns again each night, and the border folk sleep a little easier.
middle.failure: A border beacon manned by the realm's own people had gone unlit for a week. Nobody could settle who was meant to light it, so it burns some nights and not others, and the border folk don't trust it.
middle.criticalFailure: A border beacon manned by the realm's own people had gone unlit for a week. While the council argued over whose job it was, raiders slipped past it in the dark, and the border villages blame the crown for leaving them blind.

late.criticalSuccess: Scouts had found a whole stretch of the border with no tower manned. Within the month every empty tower had a garrison, the scouts who raised the alarm were promoted, and the frontier has never been better watched.
late.success: Scouts had found a whole stretch of the border with no tower manned. Garrisons were marched out to every empty tower, some of them green recruits who jump at owls, but the blind stretch of frontier has eyes again.
late.failure: Scouts had found a stretch of border with every tower empty. A few towers got men, but not enough, and anyone who wants to slip through the gap still can.
late.criticalFailure: Scouts had found a stretch of border with every tower empty, and while orders went back and forth the towers stayed that way. Enemies of the realm noticed first, and the frontier folk feel abandoned.

early.criticalSuccess: Two young recruits had fled the barracks and were hiding at their mother's farm. Someone went to the farm, shared her table and listened, and the boys came back on their own, ashamed and grateful. The barracks treat them like brothers now.
early.success: Two young recruits had fled the barracks and were hiding at their mother's farm. They were found and talked into coming back, and after a few weeks of extra chores the matter was closed.
early.failure: Two young recruits had fled the barracks and were hiding at their mother's farm. They were dragged back, but they sulk at every drill, and the other recruits wonder whether to follow them next time.
early.criticalFailure: Two young recruits had fled the barracks and were hiding at their mother's farm. The soldiers sent after them handled it roughly and the mother was hurt in the scuffle. The boys are gone for good, and the village has turned against the barracks.

middle.criticalSuccess: A company of the realm's soldiers had come up a dozen men short the morning after payday. The missing dozen were found drinking their pay in a nearby town, brought back for a fair hearing, and the company is tighter than it was before.
middle.success: A company of the realm's soldiers had come up a dozen men short the morning after payday. Once word got out there'd be a fair hearing, the missing men drifted back by twos and threes, and the company's bunks are full again.
middle.failure: A company of the realm's soldiers had come up a dozen men short the morning after payday. Only a few came back. The rest are gone with their pay, and the company is short-handed and grumbling.
middle.criticalFailure: A company of the realm's soldiers had come up a dozen men short the morning after payday. The hunt for them turned into a heavy-handed crackdown, more men slipped away the next payday, and the ones who stayed are bitter.

late.criticalSuccess: An entire company had walked off its post, claiming it was promised land and never got it. The grievance was heard in full and the land was granted at last. The soldiers marched back to their post singing, and veterans across the realm took note.
late.success: An entire company had walked off its post, claiming it was promised land and never got it. A fair settlement of the land was worked out, and though it will take time, the soldiers have returned to their post.
late.failure: An entire company had walked off its post, claiming it was promised land and never got it. They came back only after hard bargaining and harder words, and they tell anyone who'll listen that the crown can't be trusted.
late.criticalFailure: An entire company had walked off its post, claiming it was promised land and never got it. Their grievance was dismissed, and they scattered into the countryside with their weapons. Some have turned to banditry, and the rest of the army is watching.

early.criticalSuccess: A trader from Restov had surplus spears and shields he wanted gone cheap. He was talked down to a bargain price, the crates turned out better than promised, and the militia has good spears and shields for the first time.
early.success: A trader from Restov had surplus spears and shields he wanted gone cheap. They were bought at a fair price, and the militia is drilling with proper weapons instead of hay forks.
early.failure: A trader from Restov had surplus spears and shields he wanted gone cheap, but the haggling went nowhere. He sold them to someone else, and the militia makes do with pitchforks a while longer.
early.criticalFailure: A trader from Restov had surplus spears and shields he wanted gone cheap. The crates turned out full of rotten hafts and rusted iron, the money was already paid, and folks are laughing at the crown's bargain.

middle.criticalSuccess: A Mivoni smithy had offered a contract for good blades. The terms were agreed so generously that the smiths sent the first crate early as a sign of trust, and the guard's new steel is the envy of the region.
middle.success: A Mivoni smithy had offered a contract for good blades, if the terms could be agreed. After a day of friendly haggling over wine the contract was signed, and the first crates of fine steel are on their way to the guard.
middle.failure: A Mivoni smithy had offered a contract for good blades, but the talks stalled over price. The smiths sold to a rival lord instead, and the guard carries old steel a while longer.
middle.criticalFailure: A Mivoni smithy had offered a contract for good blades, but the smiths walked out of the talks offended. Now they tell every buyer in the region that the realm doesn't keep its word.

late.criticalSuccess: Envoys from a dwarven forge had offered to outfit the realm's guard, for a price and a favor. They left delighted, with a price fair to both sides and a favor that cost the realm little. The guard wears dwarven steel, and a lasting friendship has begun.
late.success: Envoys from a dwarven forge had offered to outfit the realm's guard, for a price and a favor. The price was steep and the favor will come due one day, but the steel is superb.
late.failure: Envoys from a dwarven forge had offered to outfit the realm's guard, for a price and a favor. They found the realm's offer too thin and left politely, and the chance may not come again.
late.criticalFailure: Envoys from a dwarven forge had offered to outfit the realm's guard, for a price and a favor. They were insulted at the bargaining table and left swearing never to deal with the realm again, and word of it travels fast between the forges.

early.criticalSuccess: A handful of thugs were charging travelers a copper apiece to pass a bend in the road. They were run off with a few hard words and a show of steel, and travelers bought the guards drinks for a week.
early.success: A handful of thugs were charging travelers a copper apiece to pass a bend in the road. The guard chased them off into the woods, and travelers pass that bend free again.
early.failure: A handful of thugs were charging travelers a copper apiece to pass a bend in the road. They scattered when the guard came, but crept back once it had gone, and travelers are still paying.
early.criticalFailure: A handful of thugs were charging travelers a copper apiece to pass a bend in the road. The guards sent to scare them off were beaten and robbed instead. Now the toll is two coppers, and the thugs are bragging.

middle.criticalSuccess: An organized gang had thrown a stockade across the trade road and taxed every cart. The stockade was stormed and burned, the ringleaders came back in chains, and carters cheered the guards all the way to market.
middle.success: An organized gang had thrown a stockade across the trade road and was taxing every cart. The guard pulled the stockade down and the gang scattered into the hills, and carts roll down the road without paying anyone again.
middle.failure: An organized gang had thrown a stockade across the trade road. It was pulled down, but the gang simply moved a few miles along the road and built another.
middle.criticalFailure: An organized gang had thrown a stockade across the trade road, and the attack on it was beaten back with losses. The gang has raised its toll, and merchants are avoiding the realm's roads.

late.criticalSuccess: A disgraced knight had fortified a hill and called his robbery of the caravans a lawful levy. He was brought down from his hill to answer in open court, the caravans got their money back, and the realm's justice was the talk of the river.
late.success: A disgraced knight had fortified a hill and called his robbery of the caravans a lawful levy. His hill fort was taken after a short, sharp fight, his 'levy' was ended, and the caravans roll freely again.
late.failure: A disgraced knight had fortified a hill and was robbing the caravans. He was driven off it, but escaped with his best men and his loot, and he'll turn up on some other road.
late.criticalFailure: A disgraced knight had fortified a hill and was robbing the caravans. He beat off the realm's attack and now styles himself lord of the road, and other disgraced nobles are watching to see if it works.

early.criticalSuccess: Old soldiers who fought for the realm's founding wanted their part remembered, and they were getting loud about it. A feast was held in their honor and each was named aloud for his part, and they've become the realm's loudest champions.
early.success: Old soldiers who fought for the realm's founding wanted their part remembered. They were given a proper hearing and a promise that their names will be carved in the hall, and they've quieted down. Some are even smiling.
early.failure: Old soldiers who fought for the realm's founding wanted their part remembered. They were heard, but nothing was promised, and they still grumble in the taverns that the realm forgets who built it.
early.criticalFailure: Old soldiers who fought for the realm's founding wanted their part remembered, and they were brushed aside. They've taken their complaint to every tavern in the realm, and the young recruits are listening.

middle.criticalSuccess: Wounded veterans said the treasury had forgotten the promises made to them. The old pension ledger was dug out, every coin was paid with interest, and the veterans' gratitude has spread to every barracks.
middle.success: Wounded veterans said the treasury had forgotten the promises made to them. The clerks dug out the old pension rolls and paid what was owed, a little late but in full, and the veterans grudgingly toasted the crown.
middle.failure: Wounded veterans said the treasury had forgotten its promises. They got part of what they were owed and a great many excuses, and the grumbling goes on.
middle.criticalFailure: Wounded veterans said the treasury had forgotten its promises, and the treasury denied ever making them. Crippled soldiers now beg in the streets, and everyone who passes them blames the crown.

late.criticalSuccess: Hundreds of veterans had camped outside the seat of government and refused to leave. A leader went out to them, heard them one by one, and made promises the crown has already begun to keep. They marched home in good order, and the realm saw its leaders at their best.
late.success: Hundreds of veterans had camped outside the seat of government and refused to leave. They were heard out in turn and offered an honest settlement, and after a night of arguing among themselves they packed up and went home peacefully.
late.failure: Hundreds of veterans had camped outside the seat of government. They were talked into leaving after days of tension and promises that sounded thin, and they'll be back.
late.criticalFailure: Hundreds of veterans had camped outside the seat of government, and the guards were sent to clear them. People were hurt, and the march of the wounded has become a rallying cry against the crown.

early.criticalSuccess: Riders from beyond the border had driven off a farmer's herd in the night. A posse tracked them across the border and drove the whole herd home before dawn, raiders' horses included, and the farmer tells the story at every market.
early.success: Riders from beyond the border had driven off a farmer's herd in the night. A posse followed the trampled trail at first light and brought the herd home, short only a calf or two.
early.failure: Riders from beyond the border had driven off a farmer's herd in the night. The trail went cold at the border, and the farmer got some help from the crown but never saw his cattle again.
early.criticalFailure: Riders from beyond the border had driven off a farmer's herd in the night. The posse that chased them was ambushed, and the raiders came back the next night for the rest of the village's cattle.

middle.criticalSuccess: A border patrol had clashed with foreign riders, and both sides said the other started it. A careful inquiry showed the foreign riders struck first, their own lord apologized and paid for the trouble, and the patrol were named heroes.
middle.success: A border patrol had clashed with foreign riders, and both sides said the other started it. Talks smoothed it over. Neither side is happy, but nobody else will die over it.
middle.failure: A border patrol had clashed with foreign riders, and both sides said the other started it. It was settled without either side admitting fault, and the patrols glare at each other across the line, waiting for the next spark.
middle.criticalFailure: A border patrol had clashed with foreign riders, and both sides said the other started it. The quarrel became a blood feud between the patrols, more riders have been killed, and the border folk are packing up to leave.

late.criticalSuccess: A neighbor's cavalry had been testing the border forts one at a time. When they struck next, the fort was ready and the charge broke against its walls. They've pulled back, and the forts stand stronger for the test.
late.success: A neighbor's cavalry had been testing the realm's border forts one at a time. The forts were reinforced and held firm against the next probe, and the riders have stopped coming, for now.
late.failure: A neighbor's cavalry had been testing the border forts. The forts held, but the riders found the weak points and know them now, and the whole border is jumpy.
late.criticalFailure: A neighbor's cavalry had been testing the border forts, and one of them fell with its garrison taken. The frontier is open, and the realm looks weak to everyone watching.

early.criticalSuccess: The village fair wanted a fighting contest and someone to keep it from becoming a brawl. The bouts were fierce but fair, the crowd roared, and the winner was a shy shepherd girl nobody will ever forget.
early.success: The village fair wanted a fighting contest and someone to keep it from turning into a brawl. The quarterstaff bouts were loud and hard-fought but stayed friendly, and everyone went home with bruises, bragging rights and a good story.
early.failure: The village fair wanted a quarterstaff contest without a brawl, but by the third round it was a brawl. It was broken up quickly, and the fair ended early and sour.
early.criticalFailure: The village fair wanted a quarterstaff contest without a brawl, and instead got a riot between two villages. Stalls were wrecked, a boy was badly hurt, and next year's fair is in doubt.

middle.criticalSuccess: Brevic knights had asked to hold a tourney on the realm's fields. The lists were splendid, the realm's own champion unhorsed their best, and Brevoy will be talking about it for a year.
middle.success: Brevic knights had asked to hold a tourney on the realm's fields. The lists were well kept and the jousts went off without a hitch, the knights enjoyed themselves, and they spent good coin in the realm's inns.
middle.failure: Brevic knights had asked to hold a tourney on the realm's fields, but rain turned the lists to mud and the knights complained about everything. Few of them will come back.
middle.criticalFailure: Brevic knights had asked to hold a tourney on the realm's fields, and a knight was killed in the lists. The Brevic lords blame the realm's poor arrangements, and it has become a diplomatic sore.

late.criticalSuccess: Champions from across the River Kingdoms had come to compete in the capital. They clashed before roaring crowds, the tourney was the event of the season, and the realm's name rang from Mivon to Pitax.
late.success: Champions from across the River Kingdoms had come to compete in the capital. The Tourney of Champions filled the streets with visitors and the stands with cheering crowds, and the inns did a year's trade in a week.
late.failure: Champions from across the River Kingdoms had come to compete in the capital, but the tourney was a muddle of scheduling quarrels and half-empty stands. The champions left unimpressed.
late.criticalFailure: Champions from across the River Kingdoms had come to compete in the capital, and the final ended in a brawl between rival nations' fighters that spilled into the streets. The capital was damaged and the realm embarrassed.

early.criticalSuccess: A hedge witch swore she hadn't cursed her neighbor's goats, though the goats seemed to say otherwise. They turned out to have been eating a bitter weed, the witch was cleared, and she and her neighbor now share a pot of tea every market day.
early.success: A hedge witch swore she hadn't cursed her neighbor's goats. The matter was looked into and she was found innocent. The neighbors aren't friends, but they've stopped feuding.
early.failure: A hedge witch swore she hadn't cursed her neighbor's goats. No one could prove what was wrong with them, and the witch and her neighbor still glare at each other over the fence.
early.criticalFailure: A hedge witch swore she hadn't cursed her neighbor's goats, but the village decided she was guilty and drove her from her cottage. Now folks wonder who'll be next.

middle.criticalSuccess: Two spellcasters' rivalry had soured a town's wells, and each blamed the other. They were made to cleanse the wells together, found they worked better as a pair, and the rivalry has turned into a friendship.
middle.success: Two spellcasters' rivalry had soured a town's wells, and each blamed the other. Both were ordered to cleanse the wells together and keep their quarrel civil, and the water runs clean again, though they still don't speak.
middle.failure: Two spellcasters' rivalry had soured a town's wells. The wells were cleaned, but each is still certain the other did it, and the quarrel goes on.
middle.criticalFailure: Two spellcasters' rivalry had soured a town's wells, and their duel finally broke out in the town square. Windows shattered, people ran, and both swore revenge.

late.criticalSuccess: Two wizards' feud was leaving scorched streets and frightened townsfolk. They were brought before the crown, made to swear peace and set to mend the streets they'd burned, and they did it so well the town is better for it.
late.success: Two wizards' feud was leaving scorched streets and frightened townsfolk. They were ordered to stop and made to pay for every burned shutter, and the streets are safe to walk again.
late.failure: Two wizards' feud was leaving scorched streets behind it. They agreed to a truce, but fresh scorch marks keep appearing on the cobbles at night.
late.criticalFailure: Two wizards' feud was leaving scorched streets behind it, and it finally exploded into a duel that burned a whole street. The frightened townsfolk blame the crown for waiting.

early.criticalSuccess: A dying scholar wanted their books to go somewhere they'd be read. The books were given a place of honor in the village hall, and the scholar lived to see children reading them, and called it the happiest day of their life.
early.success: A dying scholar wanted their books to go somewhere they'd be read. A shelf was cleared for them in the village hall, and the scholar was glad to hear the children had started borrowing them.
early.failure: A dying scholar wanted their books to go somewhere they'd be read. They were taken in, but they sit unopened in a damp storeroom.
early.criticalFailure: A dying scholar wanted their books to go somewhere they'd be read. The cart carrying them overturned in a river, the books were lost, and the scholar died heartbroken.

middle.criticalSuccess: A Restov archive was selling off a collection the realm's scholars badly wanted. It was bought at a good price and held rare texts nobody knew were there, and the scholars are ecstatic.
middle.success: A Restov archive was selling off a collection the realm's scholars badly wanted. It was bought at a fair price and hauled home by cart, and the scholars have years of study ahead of them.
middle.failure: A Restov archive was selling off a collection the realm's scholars wanted, but someone else bought the best of it first. What's left isn't worth much.
middle.criticalFailure: A Restov archive was selling off a collection the realm's scholars wanted. It was bought, the texts turned out to be forgeries, and the realm's scholars are being mocked across the region.

late.criticalSuccess: Scholars had found a library buried under an old ruin. It was dug out safely and its books preserved, and scholars from across the Inner Sea are coming to see it.
late.success: Scholars had found a library buried under an old ruin, if it could be dug out safely. The dig went slowly and carefully, the shelves were reached intact, and the books are being restored one page at a time.
late.failure: Scholars had found a library buried under an old ruin, but part of it collapsed during the dig. Some books were saved, but much was lost.
late.criticalFailure: Scholars had found a library buried under an old ruin, and the dig woke something that had been sleeping there. The workers fled, and the ruin is cursed.

early.criticalSuccess: Floating lights over the marsh had been spooking herders and their animals. They turned out to be harmless glowing moths, and now the herders take their children to watch them on summer nights.
early.success: Floating lights over the marsh had been spooking herders and their animals. Someone went out to look and found marsh gas and fireflies, mostly harmless, and the herders have calmed down.
early.failure: Floating lights over the marsh had been spooking herders and their animals. Nobody could say what they were, and the animals still bolt at night.
early.criticalFailure: Floating lights over the marsh had been spooking herders. Someone went out to find them and never came back, and now the herders won't go near the bog.

middle.criticalSuccess: The marsh lights had been drawing people out into the bog, and two hadn't come back. The witchfire was traced to a will-o'-wisp's lair and destroyed, the missing pair were found alive, and the marsh is safe.
middle.success: The marsh lights had been drawing people out into the bog, and two hadn't come back. The will-o'-wisps behind them were found and driven off, and the lights over the bog have gone dark.
middle.failure: The marsh lights had been drawing people out into the bog. They were driven back but not gone, and a few still flicker over the water at night.
middle.criticalFailure: The marsh lights had been drawing people out into the bog, and the hunt for them lost three more people to it. Folks are terrified.

late.criticalSuccess: Ribbons of raw magic had been flickering over the realm at night, wilting the crops where they touched. They were traced to a torn ley line and it was sealed, the crops recovered, and the night sky is calm.
late.success: Ribbons of raw magic had been flickering over the realm at night, wilting crops where they touched down. Spellcasters worked through the nights to calm them, and the crops have stopped wilting.
late.failure: Ribbons of raw magic had been flickering over the realm at night. They were dimmed but not stopped, and the sky still flares on some nights.
late.criticalFailure: Ribbons of raw magic had been flickering over the realm at night, and the attempt to quell them made them worse. Crops are dying across whole provinces.

early.criticalSuccess: An apprentice's cantrip had set a barn alight. The apprentice rebuilt it by hand with a lesson in fire safety for the whole village, and the farmer swears it's the finest barn in the realm.
early.success: An apprentice's cantrip had set a barn alight. The apprentice's master paid for a new barn and the apprentice spent a month helping build it, and he's studying much more carefully now.
early.failure: An apprentice's cantrip had set a barn alight. The farmer got some coin for it, but not enough, and he's still sore about it.
early.criticalFailure: An apprentice's cantrip had set a barn alight, and the fire spread to two more. The village wants every spellcaster gone.

middle.criticalSuccess: A summoned creature had got loose in the market and wouldn't go back. It was coaxed home without anyone getting hurt, and the stalls were selling souvenirs of the day by evening.
middle.success: A summoned creature had got loose in the market and wouldn't go back. After a chase through the stalls and a lot of broken crockery, it was sent back where it came from.
middle.failure: A summoned creature had got loose in the market. It was caught in the end, but not before it wrecked half the stalls.
middle.criticalFailure: A summoned creature had got loose in the market, and it hurt several people before it was destroyed. Folks don't want summoners in town.

late.criticalSuccess: A failed ritual had torn the air of a wizard's tower, and things were coming through. The tear was sealed and the things driven back, and the tower's master swore never to try such a ritual again.
late.success: A failed ritual had left a tear in the air of a wizard's tower, and things were coming through. The rift was sewn shut after a long night, and the things that came through were hunted down.
late.failure: A failed ritual had torn the air of a wizard's tower. The rift was closed, but some of what came through slipped away into the countryside.
late.criticalFailure: A failed ritual had torn the air of a wizard's tower, and the rift widened before it could be closed. Things poured through into the town.

early.criticalSuccess: A farmer who watched the stars had offered to write a planting almanac. It was printed and handed out, the next harvest came in early and plentiful, and every farmhouse keeps a copy by the hearth.
early.success: A farmer who watched the stars had offered to write a planting almanac for the realm. It was copied and handed out at market, and more and more farms are planting by its dates.
early.failure: A farmer who watched the stars had offered to write a planting almanac. It was written, but few farmers trust a neighbor's stargazing over their grandfathers' habits.
early.criticalFailure: A farmer who watched the stars had written a planting almanac, but his dates were wrong. The fields were planted too early, and the frost took them.

middle.criticalSuccess: An astrologer wanted to build an observatory and needed a patron. With the crown's backing it was built, its first predictions came true, and scholars are flocking to it.
middle.success: An astrologer wanted to build an observatory and needed a patron. The crown paid for the tower and the lenses, and the astrologer spends every clear night up there at work.
middle.failure: An astrologer wanted to build an observatory and needed a patron. Work began, but it was never finished, and it stands half built on the hill.
middle.criticalFailure: An astrologer wanted to build an observatory and needed a patron. He took the crown's coin and vanished, and folks are laughing at how easily the crown was fooled.

late.criticalSuccess: Scholars had predicted a rare conjunction. The realm prepared well, and when it came the rituals drew a blessing that will rest on the land for a generation.
late.success: Scholars had predicted a rare conjunction, and a realm that prepared for it could gain a great deal. The realm was ready when it came, the rituals went well, and some of that power was caught and kept.
late.failure: Scholars had predicted a rare conjunction, and the realm prepared for it, but the right moment was missed. Little came of all the work.
late.criticalFailure: Scholars had predicted a rare conjunction, and the rituals for it went horribly wrong. A burst of wild magic scorched the observatory and everyone near it.

early.criticalSuccess: An old coin from a field was bringing bad luck to everyone who held it. It was blessed and buried at a crossroads, the bad luck lifted at once, and the farmer who found it won the next fair's prize pig.
early.success: An old coin had turned up in a field, and everyone who held it had a run of bad luck. A priest took it away and buried it somewhere no one will find, and the bad luck went with it.
early.failure: An old coin from a field was bringing bad luck to everyone who held it. It was thrown in the river, but folks swear the bad luck lingers.
early.criticalFailure: An old coin from a field was bringing bad luck to everyone who held it, and it went missing before it could be dealt with. Now nobody knows who has it.

middle.criticalSuccess: A mirror sold at market was wearing its owners thin one by one. It was shattered under a priest's blessing, its victims recovered, and the market is a cheerful place again.
middle.success: A mirror sold at market was wearing its owners thin, one by one. It was traced from buyer to buyer and smashed before it could take anyone else.
middle.failure: A mirror sold at market was wearing its owners thin. It was found and locked away, but too late for its last owner.
middle.criticalFailure: A mirror sold at market was wearing its owners thin. It was found and seized, then stolen from the crown's own vault, and it's still out there.

late.criticalSuccess: A relic from a long-gone kingdom had woken, and blight was spreading around it. It was laid to rest with the proper rites, the blight withered away, and the land around it is greener than ever.
late.success: A relic from a kingdom long gone had woken, and blight was spreading around it. It was sealed in lead and stone, and the blight has stopped creeping outward.
late.failure: A relic from a long-gone kingdom had woken and was spreading blight. It was contained, but the blight still clings to the land around it.
late.criticalFailure: A relic from a long-gone kingdom had woken, and its blight spread across the province before it could be contained.

early.criticalSuccess: Parents wanted a teacher for their children and a room to teach in. A teacher was found and a room set aside, every child in the village is learning their letters, and the parents are proud and grateful.
early.success: Parents wanted a teacher for their children and a room to teach in. The back room of the hall was given over to it, a teacher was found, and the children are learning their letters.
early.failure: Parents wanted a teacher for their children and a room to teach in. A room was found, but no teacher stayed long, and the children are back in the fields.
early.criticalFailure: Parents wanted a teacher for their children and a room to teach in. The room's roof caved in on the first day, and though nobody was badly hurt, the parents are furious.

middle.criticalSuccess: Scholars had asked for a charter to found an academy. It was granted, the academy opened its doors, and its first students made a name for the realm within the year.
middle.success: A group of scholars had asked for a charter to found an academy. The charter was granted, a house was found for it, and the academy has opened its doors to its first students.
middle.failure: Scholars had asked for a charter to found an academy, but the charter got tangled in arguments, and the academy hasn't opened yet.
middle.criticalFailure: Scholars had asked for a charter to found an academy, then fell out over who would lead it. The whole thing collapsed in bitterness.

late.criticalSuccess: Learned societies from three nations wanted to found a university in the capital. It was founded with all three, and it's already the pride of the River Kingdoms.
late.success: Learned societies from three nations wanted to found a university in the capital. It was founded with all three on its council, and students are arriving from across the region.
late.failure: Learned societies from three nations wanted to found a university in the capital, but only one stayed the course. It's a small affair.
late.criticalFailure: Learned societies from three nations wanted to found a university in the capital, then fell out with the crown and took their plans elsewhere. The realm looks backward.

early.criticalSuccess: A sprite was demanding a bowl of milk from everyone who crossed a certain bridge. She was offered a feast instead, and she was so delighted that she now blesses everyone who crosses.
early.success: A sprite was demanding a bowl of milk from everyone who crossed a certain bridge. A fair bargain was struck: a jug left at the bridge each full moon, and folks cross in peace.
early.failure: A sprite was demanding a bowl of milk from everyone who crossed a certain bridge. She was bargained with, but she still pinches anyone who forgets the milk.
early.criticalFailure: A sprite was demanding a bowl of milk from everyone who crossed a certain bridge. She was insulted in the talks, and the bridge collapsed the next morning.

middle.criticalSuccess: Parents in one village were certain their children had been swapped. It turned out to be a fey prank, the true children were brought home with gifts from the fey, and the village celebrates the day every year.
middle.success: Parents in one village were certain their children had been swapped by the fey. A priest and a hedge witch looked over every child and found nothing amiss, and the parents are satisfied their children are their own.
middle.failure: Parents in one village were certain their children had been swapped. The rumors died down, but some parents still watch their children with doubt.
middle.criticalFailure: Parents in one village were certain their children had been swapped, and the rumors turned into a witch hunt. Children were harmed.

late.criticalSuccess: A fey noble had arrived to collect an old debt from the land itself. It was paid with cleverness instead of land, and he left with a blessing that will last for generations.
late.success: A fey noble had arrived to collect an old debt from the land itself. After long, strange talks the debt was settled at a fair price, and he went back to his own realm without taking anything that mattered.
late.failure: A fey noble had arrived to collect an old debt from the land. It was settled, but it cost far more than anyone wanted.
late.criticalFailure: A fey noble had arrived to collect an old debt from the land, and he took his due from the land itself. Fields withered wherever he walked.

early.criticalSuccess: Farmers had wanted a proper ditch dug to water the lower fields. The whole village turned out with shovels and cut it in a week, and the lower fields gave the best harvest anyone can remember.
early.success: Farmers wanted a proper ditch dug to water the lower fields. Neighbors pitched in with shovels for a fortnight, and water runs into the lower fields at last.
early.failure: Farmers had wanted a proper ditch dug to water the lower fields. It was dug, but too shallow, and the water barely reaches them.
early.criticalFailure: Farmers had wanted a proper ditch dug to water the lower fields. It was cut in the wrong place, flooded a neighbor's field and washed out his seed.

middle.criticalSuccess: Millers had wanted a race cut from the river to turn a second wheel. The race was dug and the wheel turned within the month, flour is cheaper, and the millers are toasting the crown.
middle.success: Millers wanted a race cut from the river to turn a second wheel. The race was dug and lined with stone, and the second wheel turns, grinding twice the flour.
middle.failure: Millers had wanted a race cut from the river to turn a second wheel. It was dug, but the water runs too slow to turn the wheel well.
middle.criticalFailure: Millers had wanted a race cut from the river to turn a second wheel. The race broke through its banks and washed away part of the old mill.

late.criticalSuccess: Engineers had proposed a canal to water a whole valley. It was dug and filled, the valley bloomed like a garden, and farmers came from across the realm to settle along its banks.
late.success: Engineers had proposed a canal that would water a whole valley. After a long season of digging the canal was filled, and the valley's dry fields are green for the first time in years.
late.failure: Engineers had proposed a canal to water a whole valley. It was dug, but leaks and silt mean it waters only half the valley.
late.criticalFailure: Engineers had proposed a canal to water a whole valley. Its walls failed in the first flood, and the water drowned the fields it was meant to save.

early.criticalSuccess: Orange rust had been spreading through one farmer's wheat. It was caught early and burned out before it reached a single neighbor's field, and the farmers are calling it a lucky escape.
early.success: Orange rust was spreading through one farmer's wheat, and the neighbors were worried. His field was burned before it could spread, the crown paid him for the loss, and the neighbors' wheat is safe.
early.failure: Orange rust had been spreading through one farmer's wheat. It was burned, but it had already reached the next farm, and both families will go short.
early.criticalFailure: Orange rust had been spreading through one farmer's wheat, and nobody acted in time. It's in every field in the village, and the harvest is ruined.

middle.criticalSuccess: A rot had been moving from field to field faster than anyone could burn it. A clever herbalist found what stops it, the fields were saved, and folks have made her a local hero.
middle.success: A rot was moving from field to field faster than anyone could burn it. Ditches were dug and the infected fields burned, and the rot was stopped before it reached any more farms.
middle.failure: A rot had been moving from field to field faster than anyone could burn it. It slowed, but it took several farms before it did.
middle.criticalFailure: A rot had been moving from field to field faster than anyone could burn it, and it ran wild across the farmland. The town will be hungry this winter.

late.criticalSuccess: A blight had blackened crops across a whole region. A cure was found and spread, the next crops came up green and strong, and the realm's farmers will remember it for generations.
late.success: A blight had blackened crops across a whole region. The healthy fields were walled off with fire and ditch, the blight stopped spreading, and the region's fields will recover next year.
late.failure: A blight had blackened crops across a whole region. It was slowed, but much of the region's crop was lost.
late.criticalFailure: A blight had blackened crops across a whole region, and it spread to the next one before it could be stopped. Famine looms.

early.criticalSuccess: Spring floods had taken the footbridge to the mill, and the long way round was very long. A new one was built in a week, stronger and wider than the old, and the miller held a feast on it for everyone who helped.
early.success: Spring floods had taken the footbridge to the mill, and the long way round was very long. A new footbridge was built in a week, and folks can get their grain to the mill again.
early.failure: Spring floods had taken the footbridge to the mill. A new one went up, but it's rickety, and only the brave cross it.
early.criticalFailure: Spring floods had taken the footbridge to the mill, and the replacement collapsed with a farmer on it. He survived, but the village is furious.

middle.criticalSuccess: A stone bridge on the trade road had cracked through, with carts still using it. It was shored up and rebuilt in stone, carts roll across it safer than ever, and merchants praise the crown for acting fast.
middle.success: A stone bridge on the trade road had cracked through, and carts were still using it. Masons shored it up and rebuilt the broken arch before it could give way.
middle.failure: A stone bridge on the trade road had cracked through. It was patched, but the crack is still there, and carters cross it with a prayer.
middle.criticalFailure: A stone bridge on the trade road had cracked through, and it gave way under a loaded cart. People died, and trade on the road has stopped.

late.criticalSuccess: A major bridge had fallen into the Sellen, and trade on that road had stopped. A grand new span went up in record time, trade flows faster than before, and the bridge has become a landmark.
late.success: A major bridge had fallen into the Sellen, and trade on that road had stopped. A new bridge was raised over the summer, and wagons are rolling across it again.
late.failure: A major bridge had fallen into the Sellen. A ferry was set up where it stood, but it's slow, and trade has suffered.
late.criticalFailure: A major bridge had fallen into the Sellen, and the rebuilding was botched. The road has been dead for months.

early.criticalSuccess: The village had wanted to hold its first proper market day. It drew farmers and peddlers from three valleys, the square was full of music and haggling, and it's going to be a monthly event.
early.success: The village wanted to hold its first proper market day. Stalls went up in the square, peddlers came from the next valley, and folks had a fine day haggling and gossiping.
early.failure: The village had wanted to hold its first proper market day, but it rained, and only a few stalls bothered to set up.
early.criticalFailure: The village had wanted to hold its first proper market day, and a fight broke out and turned the stalls over. Nobody wants to try again.

middle.criticalSuccess: Farmers had wanted a harvest fair to sell their surplus and show off their best animals. The best beasts took prizes, the surplus sold well, and the farmers went home rich and happy.
middle.success: Farmers wanted a harvest fair to sell their surplus and show off their best animals. The fair drew a good crowd, the prize ribbons went to the fattest pigs, and most of the surplus sold.
middle.failure: Farmers had wanted a harvest fair to sell their surplus. The fair was small and quiet, and many went home with their carts still full.
middle.criticalFailure: Farmers had wanted a harvest fair to show off their best animals, and a sickness ran through the prize pens. The fair was ruined, and the farmers blame the crown.

late.criticalSuccess: Merchants from across the region had asked to hold a great fair in the realm's lands. It was a sensation, and the realm's coffers overflowed.
late.success: Merchants from across the region had asked to hold a great fair in the realm's lands. The fair went smoothly from opening day to close, and the merchants spent good coin while they were here.
late.failure: Merchants from across the region had asked to hold a great fair, but it was a muddle of quarrels, and many left early.
late.criticalFailure: Merchants from across the region had come for a great fair, and a band of thieves robbed it blind. They're telling everyone the realm can't keep them safe.

early.criticalSuccess: The village well smelled wrong, and two families had fallen sick. A dead badger was found in the shaft, the well was cleaned and blessed, the sick recovered, and the water tastes sweeter than ever.
early.success: The village well smelled wrong, and two families had fallen sick. It was drained and scrubbed, a dead animal was hauled out of it, and the sick are getting better.
early.failure: The village well smelled wrong, and two families had fallen sick. It was cleaned, but the water still tastes off, and folks are walking to the stream instead.
early.criticalFailure: The village well smelled wrong, and two families had fallen sick. It wasn't dealt with in time, and the sickness has spread to half the village.

middle.criticalSuccess: The town's cisterns were breeding sickness, and nobody remembered who built them. They were found, drained and rebuilt, the sickness vanished, and the town has never been healthier.
middle.success: The town's cisterns were breeding sickness, and nobody remembered who built them. They were drained, scrubbed and limed, and the sickness has stopped spreading.
middle.failure: The town's cisterns were breeding sickness. They were cleaned, but folks are still falling sick now and then.
middle.criticalFailure: The town's cisterns were breeding sickness, and they weren't cleaned in time. The sickness has swept through the town.

late.criticalSuccess: Something was fouling the aqueduct that fed a whole city. It was found and destroyed, the water runs clean again, and the city celebrated with a festival of fountains.
late.success: Something was fouling the aqueduct that fed a whole city. Workers found a rotting carcass lodged in a culvert and cleared it, and the city's water is safe to drink again.
late.failure: Something was fouling the aqueduct that fed a whole city. It was cleared, but the water is still cloudy, and many are sick.
late.criticalFailure: Something was fouling the aqueduct that fed a whole city, and the poison spread faster than it could be stopped. Sickness has swept through the city.

early.criticalSuccess: A family from Brevoy had arrived with a wagon and wanted land to work. They were given good land by the river and had a farm built by midsummer, and their letters home are bringing more settlers.
early.success: A family from Brevoy had arrived with a wagon and wanted land to work. They were given a plot near the village, and by the first frost they had a roof over their heads.
early.failure: A family from Brevoy had arrived with a wagon and wanted land to work. They were given poor, stony land, and they're struggling to make a living from it.
early.criticalFailure: A family from Brevoy had arrived with a wagon and wanted land to work, and they were turned away. They've told everyone back home the realm isn't welcoming.

middle.criticalSuccess: A caravan of settlers had asked where they might build. They were given land and help raising houses, a new village rose within the season, and its people are fiercely loyal to the crown.
middle.success: A caravan of settlers had asked where they might build. They were shown good land by a stream, and a new hamlet is going up there.
middle.failure: A caravan of settlers had asked where they might build. They were given land, but squabbles over who got what drove some of them away.
middle.criticalFailure: A caravan of settlers had asked where they might build, and they were given land someone else already claimed. There's been fighting, and the settlers have scattered.

late.criticalSuccess: Thousands fleeing war in a neighboring land had come to the border asking to stay. They were welcomed and settled across the realm, and they've repaid the kindness with hard work and loyalty.
late.success: Thousands fleeing war in a neighboring land had come to the border asking to stay. They were let in and spread across the realm's villages, and they're starting new lives.
late.failure: Thousands fleeing war had come to the border asking to stay. They were let in, but there wasn't enough land or food, and many are struggling.
late.criticalFailure: Thousands fleeing war had come to the border asking to stay, and they were turned away. Many died at the border, and the realm's name is in tatters.

early.criticalSuccess: Wolves had been taking sheep from the high pastures. They were tracked to their den and driven off, the shepherds haven't lost a lamb since, and they've named the hunter's dog after the crown.
early.success: Wolves had been taking sheep from the high pastures. Hunters and dogs drove the pack off into the far hills, and the shepherds haven't lost a lamb since.
early.failure: Wolves had been taking sheep from the high pastures. A few were killed, but the pack is still taking lambs.
early.criticalFailure: Wolves had been taking sheep from the high pastures, and a hunter was killed going after them. The pack is bolder than ever.

middle.criticalSuccess: Something large had been killing livestock and leaving no tracks. It was revealed as a shapeshifted beast and slain, and the farmers held a feast in thanks.
middle.success: Something large had been killing livestock and leaving no tracks. Hunters staked out the pastures for a week until they caught it, a great cat that hunted from the trees, and killed it.
middle.failure: Something large had been killing livestock and leaving no tracks. It was driven off, but nobody's sure it won't come back.
middle.criticalFailure: Something large had been killing livestock and leaving no tracks, and it killed the hunters sent after it. It's still out there.

late.criticalSuccess: A wyvern had nested above the best grazing in the realm. It was slain in its nest and its hide hangs in the capital, the pastures are safe, and the realm's hunters are famous.
late.success: A wyvern had made its nest above the best grazing in the realm. Hunters smoked it out and drove it off over the mountains, and the herds are back on the pastures.
late.failure: A wyvern had nested above the best grazing in the realm. It was wounded but not driven off, and the herders keep their animals close.
late.criticalFailure: A wyvern had nested above the best grazing in the realm, and it killed the hunting party and burned the pastures. The herders are fleeing.

early.criticalSuccess: Half the village roofs leaked, and the thatcher was booked through spring. The village pitched in alongside him, every roof was patched before the rains, and the village has never been so dry or so proud.
early.success: Half the village roofs leaked, and the thatcher was booked through spring. Extra hands were found to help him, and the village is dry again.
early.failure: Half the village roofs leaked, and the thatcher was booked through spring. Some were fixed, but many still leak, and folks are sleeping wet.
early.criticalFailure: Half the village roofs leaked, and before they could be fixed one gave way in a storm. A family lost their home, and the village is angry.

middle.criticalSuccess: A fire had torn through crowded housing, and people needed roofs before the cold. Every family was housed before winter in homes sturdier than the old tenements, and folks are grateful.
middle.success: A fire had torn through crowded housing, and people needed roofs before the cold came. Temples and barns were opened and new houses framed, and every family had shelter before winter.
middle.failure: A fire had torn through crowded housing, and people needed roofs before the cold. Some got them, but many are still out in it.
middle.criticalFailure: A fire had torn through crowded housing, and its survivors were left to fend for themselves. Many fell sick in the cold.

late.criticalSuccess: A whole district of the city was slowly sinking into soft ground. Clever engineering shored it up, the district is safer than it's ever been, and engineers from across the region are studying it.
late.success: A whole district of the city was slowly sinking into soft ground. Engineers drove piles beneath the worst buildings, and the district has stopped sinking.
late.failure: A whole district of the city was slowly sinking into soft ground. The sinking was slowed, but some buildings are still leaning.
late.criticalFailure: A whole district of the city was slowly sinking into soft ground, and part of it collapsed. People were buried in the rubble.

early.criticalSuccess: The line of petitioners at the door stretched round the building, and folks were tired of waiting. The doors were thrown open, benches and cider brought out, and every one of them was heard before dark. They left feeling the crown truly listens.
early.success: The line of petitioners at the door stretched round the building, and folks were tired of waiting. The line was worked through steadily, and everyone had been heard by nightfall, tired but satisfied.
early.failure: The line of petitioners at the door stretched round the building. It crept along all day, and when the doors shut at dusk half were still waiting outside. They went home grumbling that the crown can't be bothered.
early.criticalFailure: The line of petitioners at the door stretched round the building, and after hours of waiting they were told to come back another day. Someone threw a stone, the guards pushed back, and the story of the closed door is all over the village.

middle.criticalSuccess: Every village had sent someone with a complaint, and they all wanted to be heard the same afternoon. Every one was heard on Grievance Day, a few were fixed on the spot, and the delegates rode home singing the crown's praises.
middle.success: Every village had sent someone with a complaint, and they all wanted to be heard the same afternoon. Grievance Day ran long and loud, but each village had its say and went home with an answer.
middle.failure: Every village had sent someone with a complaint for Grievance Day, but the afternoon ran out before the complaints did. The villages that weren't heard feel slighted.
middle.criticalFailure: Every village had sent someone with a complaint for Grievance Day, and it became a shouting match between them. The hearing was called off, and the delegates went home angrier than they came.

late.criticalSuccess: A petition with a thousand marks demanded the crown hear it in public. It was read in the open square and the crown answered each demand in plain words, the crowd cheered, and folks are calling it the finest day of the reign.
late.success: A petition with a thousand marks demanded the crown hear it in public. It was read aloud in the square and answered point by point, and the crowd went home mostly content.
late.failure: A petition with a thousand marks demanded the crown hear it in public. It was heard, but the answers were vague, and the crowd left muttering.
late.criticalFailure: A petition with a thousand marks demanded the crown hear it in public, and the crown refused. The thousand marks have become ten thousand, and some are talking of more than petitions.

early.criticalSuccess: Someone was telling the taverns that the leaders were skimming the grain stores. The stores were thrown open for anyone to count, the story died overnight, and the gossip who started it bought the next round to save face.
early.success: Someone was spreading a story in the taverns that the leaders were skimming the grain stores. An honest count of the stores was posted on the tavern doors, and the story faded.
early.failure: Someone was telling the taverns that the leaders were skimming the grain stores. It was denied, but denials are dull and the story is fun, and it's still going round.
early.criticalFailure: Someone was telling the taverns that the leaders were skimming the grain stores, and the crown's angry denial made it sound true. Every tavern in the realm is telling it now.

middle.criticalSuccess: Well-written unsigned pamphlets were accusing the council of crimes. The pamphleteer was unmasked as a rival's hired pen, the crown's own pamphlet laid out every lie, and folks trust the council more than before.
middle.success: Well-written unsigned pamphlets were accusing the council of crimes. Each charge was answered point by point in a pamphlet of the crown's own, and the town has stopped believing them.
middle.failure: Well-written unsigned pamphlets were accusing the council of crimes. They kept coming, and some of the mud has stuck.
middle.criticalFailure: Well-written unsigned pamphlets were accusing the council of crimes, and the hunt for their author became a clumsy crackdown on printers. Now the pamphlets call the council tyrants, and folks are starting to agree.

late.criticalSuccess: A noble with a thin claim to the land was quietly gathering supporters. They were won over one by one, and he slunk out of the realm without a friend. His claim is now a joke.
late.success: A noble with a thin claim to the land was quietly gathering supporters. They were drawn away one by one with favors and plain talk, and his plot has lost its teeth.
late.failure: A noble with a thin claim to the land was quietly gathering supporters. He lost a few, but he's still recruiting in secret.
late.criticalFailure: A noble with a thin claim to the land was quietly gathering supporters, and now he has a real following. Some nobles have gone over to him openly.

early.criticalSuccess: A village wanted to pick its own reeve and asked the crown to bless the choice. They chose a sensible woman, the blessing was given with a feast on the green, and she has already settled two old quarrels.
early.success: A village wanted to pick its own reeve and asked the crown to bless the choice. It chose a steady old farmer, and the crown's blessing was read out on the green.
early.failure: A village wanted to pick its own reeve and asked for the crown's blessing. It came late and grudging, and the new reeve feels unsupported.
early.criticalFailure: A village wanted to pick its own reeve and asked for the crown's blessing, and the crown overruled its choice. The reeve the crown wanted is a stranger in his own village.

middle.criticalSuccess: A growing town had asked for a charter and a council of its own. It got both, and the new council is already proving its worth with fair markets and clean streets.
middle.success: A growing town had asked for a charter and a council of its own. The charter was granted, a council was elected, and the town is running its own affairs.
middle.failure: A growing town had asked for a charter and a council of its own. The charter was granted, but so hedged with limits that the council can barely act.
middle.criticalFailure: A growing town had asked for a charter and a council of its own, and it was refused. Its leading citizens are talking about doing without the crown.

late.criticalSuccess: Delegates from every settlement had asked to meet as one assembly before the throne. They met, their counsel was heeded, and the assembly has bound the realm together like nothing before.
late.success: Delegates from every settlement had asked to meet as one assembly before the throne. They met for three days, and they went home feeling the crown had heard them.
late.failure: Delegates from every settlement had asked to meet as one assembly before the throne. They met, but it was mostly bickering, and little came of it.
late.criticalFailure: Delegates from every settlement had met as one assembly before the throne, and the assembly turned on the crown. Its list of grievances is being read in every town.

early.criticalSuccess: A village reeve was taking a cut of every fine, and the villagers knew it. He was caught red-handed, made to pay back every coin and replaced by someone the village trusts. Fines are fair again.
early.success: A village reeve was taking a cut of every fine, and the villagers knew it. He was removed from his post and made to repay what he took, and fines are fair again.
early.failure: A village reeve was taking a cut of every fine. He was warned, but he's still at it, only more carefully.
early.criticalFailure: A village reeve was taking a cut of every fine, and friends in high places cleared his name. Now he's taking a bigger cut than before.

middle.criticalSuccess: Word was that a magistrate could be bought, and cheaply. He was caught in a trap and removed, the judgments he sold were overturned, and folks believe in the courts again.
middle.success: Word was that a magistrate could be bought, and the price wasn't even high. He was removed from the bench, and his worst judgments were heard again by an honest judge.
middle.failure: Word was that a magistrate could be bought. He was removed, but nobody fixed the judgments he'd sold.
middle.criticalFailure: Word was that a magistrate could be bought, and he bought his way out of trouble. Now everyone knows justice is for sale.

late.criticalSuccess: An entire office of the government was selling favors to the highest bidder. It was cleaned out top to bottom, honest clerks were put in its place, and the government is stronger for it.
late.success: An entire office of the government was selling favors to the highest bidder. It was cleaned out, its worst officials were punished, and honest clerks are learning the work.
late.failure: An entire office of the government was selling favors. Some officials were punished, but the rot runs deep, and it'll take years to clear.
late.criticalFailure: An entire office of the government was selling favors, and its officials closed ranks and bought their way out. The rot is spreading.

early.criticalSuccess: The miller's family had asked for a leader to come and see their new wheel. The visit was warm, the wheel was praised, bread was shared, and the miller has told the story to every customer since.
early.success: The miller's family had asked for a leader to come and see their new wheel. A leader came, admired the wheel and stayed for bread and cheese, and the family was delighted.
early.failure: The miller's family had asked for a leader to come and see their new wheel. The visit was short and distracted, and the family was let down.
early.criticalFailure: The miller's family had asked for a leader to come and see their new wheel, and the visit was forgotten and cancelled at the last minute. They feel snubbed.

middle.criticalSuccess: The crown had been invited to tour the provinces and be seen by its people. Every town turned out to cheer, and the crown has never been more beloved.
middle.success: The crown had been invited to tour the provinces and be seen by its people. The progress went to every town on the list, and folks turned out to wave.
middle.failure: The crown had been invited to tour the provinces, but the progress was a muddle of late arrivals and cancelled stops. Many towns felt slighted.
middle.criticalFailure: The crown had been invited to tour the provinces, and a near-riot in one town made the royal progress look weak and foolish.

late.criticalSuccess: A season-long progress through every corner of the realm could bind it together. The crown reached every village, shook every hand it could, and folks will tell their grandchildren about the day the crown came.
late.success: A season-long progress through every corner of the realm could bind it together. The crown was seen and cheered almost everywhere it went, and the realm feels a little more like one land.
late.failure: A season-long progress was planned through every corner of the realm, but it missed many places. Some provinces feel forgotten.
late.criticalFailure: A season-long progress was planned through every corner of the realm, and it became a string of mishaps and insults. The crown is a laughingstock.

early.criticalSuccess: A barkeep had offered to pass on what she heard, for a small fee. Within a month the crown knew about a smuggling ring and a plot to rob the mill, and the fee was money well spent.
early.success: A barkeep had offered to pass on what she heard, for a small fee. She sends word every week, and the crown knows a good deal more about what goes on in the village.
early.failure: A barkeep had offered to pass on what she heard, but her news is mostly gossip and grumbling, and not worth her fee.
early.criticalFailure: A barkeep had offered to pass on what she heard, and she was found out. The village is furious that the crown spies in its taverns.

middle.criticalSuccess: A former spy had offered to build the crown a network of informants. It's up and running, it has already uncovered a plot against the crown, and the plotters still don't know how they were caught.
middle.success: A former spy had offered to build the crown a network of informants. The network is in place, and useful news is coming in from the towns.
middle.failure: A former spy had offered to build the crown a network of informants. It was built, but its reports are slow and often wrong.
middle.criticalFailure: A former spy had built the crown a network of informants, and it was exposed. Folks are furious at the crown for spying on them.

late.criticalSuccess: The spymaster had proposed a proper intelligence service. The silent office was founded, and its quiet work has foiled plots no one will ever hear about.
late.success: The spymaster had proposed a proper intelligence service, if the crown could stomach it. It was set up quietly, and the crown knows far more of what's happening across the realm.
late.failure: The spymaster had proposed a proper intelligence service. It was set up, but it's leaky and poorly run.
late.criticalFailure: The spymaster had proposed a proper intelligence service, and it was exposed before it began. A scandal about the crown's spying is all over the realm.

early.criticalSuccess: Folks kept asking who would rule if something happened to the leaders. A clear line of succession was named in public, and the gossip turned to happier things. Folks feel the realm is built to last.
early.success: Folks kept asking who would rule if something happened to the leaders, and nobody had a good answer. A plain answer was given at the next market day, and folks have stopped asking.
early.failure: Folks kept asking who would rule if something happened to the leaders. The answer was vague, and they're still worried.
early.criticalFailure: Folks kept asking who would rule if something happened to the leaders, and the leaders refused to talk about it. The rumors are getting darker.

middle.criticalSuccess: Noble houses were lining up behind different heirs before anyone had named one. The question was settled with every house's agreement, and they've rallied behind the choice.
middle.success: Noble houses were lining up behind different heirs before anyone had even named one. An heir was named, and most of the houses accepted the choice.
middle.failure: Noble houses were lining up behind different heirs. An heir was named, but some houses are sulking.
middle.criticalFailure: Noble houses were lining up behind different heirs, and the one named split them apart. Some are openly backing a rival.

late.criticalSuccess: The court had split into factions over the succession, and both were recruiting. A clever settlement reconciled them, and they've united behind the realm's future.
late.success: The court had split into factions over the succession, and both were recruiting. The factions were brought to terms, and the court has calmed.
late.failure: The court had split into factions over the succession. They agreed to a truce, but both are still recruiting in secret.
late.criticalFailure: The court had split into factions over the succession, and they came to blows. The realm is on the edge of civil war.

early.criticalSuccess: Some poachers had said they'd go straight if the crown forgave last winter's deer. They were pardoned and made gamekeepers, and not a deer has gone missing since.
early.success: Some poachers said they'd go straight if the crown forgave last winter's deer. They were forgiven, and they've hung up their snares.
early.failure: Some poachers had said they'd go straight if forgiven. They were, but a few have slipped back into their old habits.
early.criticalFailure: Some poachers had said they'd go straight if forgiven, and they took the crown's mercy for weakness. There's more poaching than ever.

middle.criticalSuccess: A bandit crew had offered to lay down its arms for a pardon and land. They took their land and became loyal farmers, the roads are safer, and the realm gained good workers.
middle.success: A bandit crew had offered to lay down its arms for a pardon and land. The crew got both, and they're clearing fields instead of robbing carts.
middle.failure: A bandit crew had offered to lay down its arms for a pardon and land. They got both, but some have drifted back to the hills.
middle.criticalFailure: A bandit crew had offered to lay down its arms for a pardon and land, and they used the land as a base for new raids.

late.criticalSuccess: A general pardon could empty the hills of outlaws or fill the towns with them. It emptied the hills, most of the outlaws became honest citizens, and the realm is safer for it.
late.success: A general pardon could empty the hills of outlaws, or fill the towns with them. Many outlaws came in from the hills and laid down their arms, and the roads are quieter.
late.failure: A general pardon was offered to the outlaws in the hills. Some came in, but many of them are causing trouble in the towns.
late.criticalFailure: A general pardon was offered to the outlaws in the hills, and it filled the towns with them. Crime has soared.

early.criticalSuccess: A troupe of players wanted somewhere to perform and a meal after. They played the barn to a packed house, the village laughed until the candles burned out, and the troupe promised to come back every year.
early.success: A troupe of players wanted somewhere to perform and a meal after. They got the barn and a hot supper, and their show had the village laughing.
early.failure: A troupe of players wanted somewhere to perform and a meal after. They performed, but few came, and they left hungry.
early.criticalFailure: A troupe of players wanted somewhere to perform, and they were accused of stealing and run out of town before the curtain went up.

middle.criticalSuccess: A Mivoni company had offered a whole season of plays if a stage could be found. The season was a triumph, and the town's new stage has become a place of pride.
middle.success: A Mivoni company had offered a whole season of plays if a stage could be found. A stage was built in the square, and folks turned out for the season.
middle.failure: A Mivoni company had offered a whole season of plays, but the stage found for them wasn't fit, and the season was cut short.
middle.criticalFailure: A Mivoni company had offered a whole season of plays, and their first play offended the town. They left early.

late.criticalSuccess: A famous playwright wanted to premiere a work about the realm's founding. It premiered to rapturous applause, it's now performed across the River Kingdoms, and the founders are legends.
late.success: A famous playwright wanted to premiere a work about the realm's founding. It opened to a full house and a long ovation, and folks are humming its songs in the streets.
late.failure: A famous playwright wanted to premiere a work about the realm's founding. It premiered, but it was dull, and few remember it.
late.criticalFailure: A famous playwright premiered a work about the realm's founding, and it made the founders look like fools. It's being performed everywhere.

early.criticalSuccess: Two congregations both claimed the village shrine and kept moving each other's candles. They agreed to share it on alternate days, even held a joint feast, and the candles stay put now.
early.success: Two congregations both claimed the village shrine and kept moving each other's candles. They were persuaded to share it on alternate days, and the candle war is over.
early.failure: Two congregations both claimed the village shrine. Nothing was settled, and the candles keep moving.
early.criticalFailure: Two congregations both claimed the village shrine, and their quarrel came to blows. The shrine was damaged in the fight.

middle.criticalSuccess: A street preacher was drawing crowds with sermons the temples called heresy. He was engaged in a public debate and won over to a gentler path, and the temples and the crowds are at peace.
middle.success: A street preacher was drawing crowds with sermons the temples called heresy. He was persuaded to tone down his sermons, and the temples have calmed.
middle.failure: A street preacher was drawing crowds with sermons the temples called heresy. He keeps preaching, and the temples are still angry.
middle.criticalFailure: A street preacher was drawing crowds with sermons the temples called heresy, and he was arrested. His followers rioted in the streets.

late.criticalSuccess: A great temple had split down the middle, and the faithful were taking sides in the streets. A council of the faithful healed the schism, and the temple is whole again.
late.success: A great temple had split down the middle, and the faithful were taking sides in the streets. The schism was settled with a compromise, and the faithful have stopped fighting.
late.failure: A great temple had split down the middle. The schism was calmed, but the temple is still divided.
late.criticalFailure: A great temple had split down the middle, and the schism became a bloody street war between the faithful.

early.criticalSuccess: The village wanted a harvest supper and a bonfire, and someone to bless the bread. It was a joy, the blessing brought tears to the old folks' eyes, and it will be a village tradition.
early.success: The village wanted a harvest supper and a bonfire, and someone to bless the bread. The supper was held and the bread blessed, and the bonfire burned late into the night.
early.failure: The village wanted a harvest supper and a bonfire, but it was a small and quiet affair.
early.criticalFailure: The village wanted a harvest supper and a bonfire, and the bonfire got out of hand and burned down the barn where the supper was held.

middle.criticalSuccess: Townsfolk wanted to float lanterns on the river for the dead, as their grandparents had. The river filled with light, folks wept as they remembered their dead, and it's become the realm's most beloved custom.
middle.success: Townsfolk wanted to float lanterns on the river for the dead, as their grandparents had. The lanterns drifted downstream in a long line of light, and the town remembered its dead.
middle.failure: Townsfolk wanted to float lanterns on the river for the dead, but few lanterns floated, and it felt half-hearted.
middle.criticalFailure: Townsfolk wanted to float lanterns on the river for the dead, and the lanterns set a riverside warehouse on fire. The festival ended in tragedy.

late.criticalSuccess: A realm-wide festival could have every settlement celebrating on the same night. It did, the whole land glowed with joy, and it's the realm's greatest holiday now.
late.success: A realm-wide festival could have every settlement celebrating on the same night. Bonfires were lit on every hill on the same night, and the settlements celebrated together.
late.failure: A realm-wide festival was planned so every settlement would celebrate on the same night, but many didn't bother, and the night felt patchy and half-hearted.
late.criticalFailure: A realm-wide festival was held, and it saw riots in several towns. It's been called off for good.
