early.criticalSuccess: A calf had been born with two heads, and the whole village thought it meant something. It was declared a sign of good fortune and given a place of honor at the fair, and the village now thinks it's the luckiest in the realm.
early.success: A calf had been born with two heads, and the whole village thought it meant something. The village priest declared it meant nothing at all, and the village calmed down.
early.failure: A calf had been born with two heads, and the village thought it meant something. Nobody could settle it, and the village is still nervous.
early.criticalFailure: A calf had been born with two heads, and the village decided it was a curse. They blame the leaders for it.

middle.criticalSuccess: A statue in the square had started weeping, and pilgrims were sleeping in the street. It was found to be a natural spring, and it became a shrine of healing where pilgrims are welcome.
middle.success: A statue in the square had started weeping, and pilgrims were sleeping in the street. A mason found water seeping through the stone, and the pilgrims went home.
middle.failure: A statue in the square had started weeping. It still weeps, and the pilgrims are still in the street.
middle.criticalFailure: A statue in the square had started weeping, and it started a cult that's causing trouble in the town.

late.criticalSuccess: A red comet hung in the sky, and every prophet in the realm had an opinion. It was declared a sign of the realm's coming glory, the prophets all agreed, and folks are hopeful.
late.success: A red comet hung in the sky, and every prophet in the realm had an opinion. The crown's astrologers explained it plainly, and folks stopped panicking.
late.failure: A red comet hung in the sky, and every prophet had an opinion. Folks are still nervous, and the prophets are still shouting.
late.criticalFailure: A red comet hung in the sky, and its prophets started riots across the realm.

early.criticalSuccess: An old woman knew every story about the land, and nobody had written them down. Her tales were set down in a fine book, the village reads them every winter, and she's become a local treasure.
early.success: An old woman knew every story about the land, and nobody had written them down. A scribe sat with her through the winter and wrote them out.
early.failure: An old woman knew every story about the land, but only a few were written down before she grew too tired to tell them.
early.criticalFailure: An old woman knew every story about the land, and she died before they could be written down. They're lost forever.

middle.criticalSuccess: A bard wanted to write the ballad of the realm's founding, if someone would tell it right. The ballad is sung in every tavern now, it gets the story just right, and the founders are heroes.
middle.success: A bard wanted to write the ballad of the realm's founding, if someone would tell it right. The story was told to her, and she made a good song of it.
middle.failure: A bard wanted to write the ballad of the realm's founding, but she got the story wrong, and nobody's quite sure how to correct a song.
middle.criticalFailure: A bard wanted to write the ballad of the realm's founding, and the one she wrote makes the founders look like fools. It's being sung everywhere.

late.criticalSuccess: Scholars and poets proposed a proper chronicle of the realm, to be read for centuries. It was written, and the realm's story will never be forgotten.
late.success: Scholars and poets proposed a proper chronicle of the realm, to be read for centuries. The chronicle was written, bound in leather and copied for every temple library.
late.failure: Scholars and poets proposed a proper chronicle of the realm. It was started, but it's a muddle of quarrelling hands.
late.criticalFailure: Scholars and poets proposed a proper chronicle of the realm, and it was written by a bitter scholar who made the founders out to be villains.

early.criticalSuccess: Someone had painted rude pictures of the leaders on the village well. They were washed off, the culprit was caught and made to paint a mural of the founding instead, and it's actually quite good.
early.success: Someone had painted rude pictures of the leaders on the village well. The paint was scrubbed off, and the culprit was caught, paint still on his hands.
early.failure: Someone had painted rude pictures of the leaders on the village well. They were cleaned off, but the culprit is still out there with a paint pot.
early.criticalFailure: Someone had painted rude pictures of the leaders on the village well, and they keep coming back. The village thinks they're funny.

middle.criticalSuccess: The founders' monument had been smashed in the night. It was rebuilt grander than before, the vandals were caught and made to work on it, and the town is proud of it.
middle.success: The founders' monument had been smashed in the night. It was repaired, and the vandals were caught bragging about it in a tavern.
middle.failure: The founders' monument had been smashed in the night. It was repaired, but the vandals were never found.
middle.criticalFailure: The founders' monument had been smashed in the night, and after it was repaired it was smashed again. The vandals are bragging.

late.criticalSuccess: A gallery of the realm's finest art had gone up in flames, and it wasn't an accident. The arsonists were caught, and a new gallery was built that's even grander than the old.
late.success: A gallery of the realm's finest art had gone up in flames, and it wasn't an accident. The arsonists were caught, and the gallery is being rebuilt.
late.failure: A gallery of the realm's finest art had gone up in flames, and it wasn't an accident. It's being rebuilt, but the arsonists were never caught.
late.criticalFailure: A gallery of the realm's finest art had gone up in flames, and the arsonists struck again before they could be caught. Another gallery burned.

early.criticalSuccess: Two families wanted a leader to stand witness at their wedding. A leader came, stood witness and danced with the bride's grandmother, and both families are bound to the crown for life.
early.success: Two families wanted a leader to stand witness at their wedding. A leader stood witness and stayed for the dancing, and the families were honored.
early.failure: Two families wanted a leader to stand witness at their wedding. The leader came late and left early.
early.criticalFailure: Two families wanted a leader to stand witness at their wedding, and the leader forgot entirely. The families feel insulted.

middle.criticalSuccess: Two noble houses were marrying and wanted the crown's blessing in public. It was given in a grand ceremony, and both houses are now the crown's staunchest allies.
middle.success: Two noble houses were marrying and wanted the crown's blessing in public. The blessing was given in the square, and both houses were pleased.
middle.failure: Two noble houses were marrying and wanted the crown's blessing in public. It was given, but half-heartedly.
middle.criticalFailure: Two noble houses were marrying and wanted the crown's blessing in public, and the ceremony went wrong. Both houses blame the crown.

late.criticalSuccess: A marriage between the court and a foreign house would be the event of the decade, and it was. The bond has made the realm a power to reckon with.
late.success: A marriage between the court and a foreign house would be the event of the decade. The royal wedding went off without a hitch, the guests feasted for three days, and the alliance is made.
late.failure: A marriage between the court and a foreign house went ahead, but it was a dull affair, and the alliance feels weak.
late.criticalFailure: A marriage between the court and a foreign house was a disaster, and the foreign house has called off the alliance.

early.criticalSuccess: The village graveyard was full, and folks didn't like the new plot by the river. A new graveyard was blessed on the hill above it instead, the village finds it beautiful, and folks are glad to rest there.
early.success: The village graveyard was full, and folks didn't like the new plot by the river. The new ground was blessed properly and given a stone wall, and folks have accepted it.
early.failure: The village graveyard was full, and folks didn't like the new plot by the river. It's still unpopular, and folks grumble about it.
early.criticalFailure: The village graveyard was full, and the new plot by the river flooded in the spring. The village is horrified.

middle.criticalSuccess: Families said their dead wouldn't rest because the rites were done wrong. The rites were done again properly, the dead are at peace, and the families are grateful.
middle.success: Families said their dead wouldn't rest because the rites had been done wrong. The rites were done again with care, and the dead are resting.
middle.failure: Families said their dead wouldn't rest because the rites were done wrong. The rites were redone, but some families still say the dead won't rest.
middle.criticalFailure: Families said their dead wouldn't rest because the rites were done wrong, and the restless dead rose from their graves. The town is terrified.

late.criticalSuccess: Old plague pits had been dug up for a new road, and the whole city was frightened. They were sealed with holy rites and the road was moved, and the city is calm and grateful.
late.success: Old plague pits had been dug up for a new road, and the whole city was frightened. The pits were filled and sealed with prayers, and the city has calmed.
late.failure: Old plague pits had been dug up for a new road. They were sealed, but folks are still frightened.
late.criticalFailure: Old plague pits had been dug up for a new road, and sickness rose from them. The city is in a panic.

early.criticalSuccess: A minor noble from Restov had written asking about trade and a visit. The letter was answered warmly with an invitation, and the visit went so well that he left with a trade deal and a promise to speak up for the realm in Restov.
early.success: A minor noble from Restov had written asking about trade and a visit. He was answered politely and welcomed, a modest trade deal came of it, and the realm has a friendly name in Restov.
early.failure: A minor noble from Restov had written asking about trade and a visit, but the letter sat unanswered too long. By the time a reply went out, he'd made his deals with someone else.
early.criticalFailure: A minor noble from Restov had written asking about trade and a visit, and the reply was so clumsy he took it as an insult. He's telling his friends in Restov the realm is run by bumpkins.

middle.criticalSuccess: An envoy from Mivon had arrived with gifts and sharp questions. She was answered with better gifts and sharper wit, and left charmed. Mivon now speaks of the realm as a friend.
middle.success: An envoy from Mivon had arrived with gifts and sharp questions. Her gifts were accepted gracefully and her questions answered well, and she left with a good report for Mivon.
middle.failure: An envoy from Mivon had arrived with gifts and sharp questions. Her questions got muddled answers, and she left with her gifts given and little to show for them.
middle.criticalFailure: An envoy from Mivon had arrived with gifts and sharp questions. Her gifts were mishandled and her questions dodged, and she left in a temper. Mivon has cooled toward the realm.

late.criticalSuccess: A great embassy from a powerful neighbor had come for a treaty, watching closely how it was treated. Its welcome was flawless, the treaty was signed on the realm's terms, and the neighbor now treats the realm as an equal.
late.success: A great embassy from a powerful neighbor had come for a treaty, watching closely how it was treated. It was received with proper honor at every step, and a fair treaty was signed.
late.failure: A great embassy from a powerful neighbor had come for a treaty, and it noticed every slip in its welcome. The talks dragged, and nothing was signed.
late.criticalFailure: A great embassy from a powerful neighbor had come for a treaty, and a careless welcome insulted it. The embassy left in fury, and the neighbor now counts the realm as a rival.

early.criticalSuccess: Someone had been cutting barges loose on the Sellen at night. A watch caught a pair of drunken bargemen doing it for a lark, and they're paying for every lost load.
early.success: Someone had been cutting barges loose on the Sellen at night. Watches were posted on the docks, the culprits were caught with knives in hand, and the cutting stopped.
early.failure: Someone had been cutting barges loose on the Sellen at night. Watches were posted, but the cutters slipped past them, and a few more barges drifted off.
early.criticalFailure: Someone had been cutting barges loose on the Sellen at night, and after a botched watch they grew bolder. Whole cargoes are vanishing now.

middle.criticalSuccess: Raiders in fast boats were hitting river traffic and vanishing downstream. A trap was baited with a rich-looking barge, they sailed right into it, and their leaders are in chains.
middle.success: Raiders in fast boats were hitting river traffic and vanishing downstream. They were chased to their hideout in the reeds and it was burned, and the river is safe again.
middle.failure: Raiders in fast boats were hitting river traffic. They lost a boat or two, but they still strike when they please.
middle.criticalFailure: Raiders in fast boats were hitting river traffic, and the attack on them went badly. They sank a patrol boat and doubled their raids out of spite.

late.criticalSuccess: A pirate captain had a fleet on the river and was calling it a kingdom. It was broken in a single campaign, his ships seized and the captain dragged to the capital in chains.
late.success: A pirate captain had a fleet on the river and was calling it a kingdom. His ships were driven off the river one by one, and his little kingdom has collapsed.
late.failure: A pirate captain had a fleet on the river and was calling it a kingdom. It was driven back, but he escaped with half his ships.
late.criticalFailure: A pirate captain had a fleet on the river and was calling it a kingdom, and he beat back the realm's boats. Now he demands tribute from every river town.

early.criticalSuccess: A border farmer swore his field belonged to the realm, and his neighbor swore it didn't. A surveyor and an old map settled it to everyone's surprise and satisfaction, and they shook hands over a jug of cider.
early.success: A border farmer swore his field belonged to the realm, and his neighbor swore it didn't. The border was walked and settled fairly, and though neither is happy, both have accepted it.
early.failure: A border farmer and his neighbor both claimed the same field. Nothing was settled, and both are still plowing the same furrows and cursing each other.
early.criticalFailure: A border farmer and his neighbor both claimed the same field, and their quarrel turned into a fistfight. One farmer's barn burned that night.

middle.criticalSuccess: Someone had moved the border stones in the night, and a neighbor's soldiers had noticed. The stones were put back with the soldiers watching, a proper boundary was agreed, and their captain even apologized.
middle.success: Someone had moved the border stones in the night, and a neighbor's soldiers had noticed. The stones were put back where they belonged with both sides watching, and the soldiers stood down.
middle.failure: Someone had moved the border stones in the night. They were put back, but the neighbor's soldiers are still watching the border closely.
middle.criticalFailure: Someone had moved the border stones in the night, and putting them back started a skirmish with the neighbor's soldiers.

late.criticalSuccess: A neighboring ruler had published a claim to one of the realm's provinces. It was torn apart with old charters and witnesses, he withdrew it in public, and the province is more firmly the realm's than ever.
late.success: A neighboring ruler had published a claim to one of the realm's provinces. Old charters answered the claim, and it has been set aside, for now.
late.failure: A neighboring ruler had published a claim to one of the realm's provinces. It was answered, but he hasn't given it up, and the province is nervous.
late.criticalFailure: A neighboring ruler had published a claim to one of the realm's provinces, and he's pressing it. Troops are moving toward the province.

early.criticalSuccess: A ferryman wanted to run a regular crossing if the crown would back him. With a new raft and the crown's coin, his crossing is so busy he's hired two helpers.
early.success: A ferryman wanted to run a regular crossing if the crown would back him. With the crown's coin he built a sturdy raft, and folks use his ferry every day.
early.failure: A ferryman wanted to run a regular crossing. It runs, but it's slow and leaky, and folks still take the long way round.
early.criticalFailure: A ferryman wanted to run a regular crossing, and his ferry capsized on its first trip. Nobody drowned, but nobody will ride it now.

middle.criticalSuccess: A boatwright proposed a packet boat between the realm's river towns. It runs on a regular schedule, and letters, goods and people move faster than ever.
middle.success: A boatwright proposed a packet boat between the realm's river towns. It runs up and down the river twice a week, and trade is picking up.
middle.failure: A boatwright proposed a packet boat between the river towns. It runs, but rarely on time.
middle.criticalFailure: A boatwright proposed a packet boat between the river towns, and it ran aground on its first run and lost its cargo.

late.criticalSuccess: Shipwrights proposed a fleet of barges to carry the realm's trade downriver. It was built, its barges reach eager markets, and the coffers are filling.
late.success: Shipwrights proposed a fleet of barges to carry the realm's trade downriver. The barges were built, and the realm's goods are flowing downriver.
late.failure: Shipwrights proposed a fleet of barges for the realm's trade. It was built, but there's not enough trade to keep it busy.
late.criticalFailure: Shipwrights proposed a fleet of barges for the realm's trade, and its first convoy sank in a storm.

early.criticalSuccess: A visiting merchant said he'd been insulted at the inn and was threatening to tell everyone. He was given a fine dinner and a sincere apology, and now he tells everyone about the realm's hospitality instead.
early.success: A visiting merchant said he'd been insulted at the inn and was threatening to tell everyone. He got an apology and a free room, and he calmed down.
early.failure: A visiting merchant said he'd been insulted at the inn. He got an apology, but he's still telling people about it.
early.criticalFailure: A visiting merchant said he'd been insulted at the inn, and he was insulted again trying to complain. Now he's telling every trader on the river.

middle.criticalSuccess: A foreign guest had been seated badly at a feast, and their country had taken notice. A second feast honored them in the place of honor, and their country sent thanks for the gesture.
middle.success: A foreign guest had been seated badly at a feast, and their country had taken notice. A fitting apology and a small gift were sent, and their country let it go.
middle.failure: A foreign guest had been seated badly at a feast. An apology was made, but their country is still cool toward the realm.
middle.criticalFailure: A foreign guest had been seated badly at a feast, and the apology was botched. Their country has recalled its people.

late.criticalSuccess: An ambassador had been humiliated in public, and war talk had started. A public apology and a lavish gift turned the war talk into talk of friendship.
late.success: An ambassador had been humiliated in public, and war talk had started. A public apology was made in the same hall, and the war talk faded.
late.failure: An ambassador had been humiliated in public. The apology was accepted, but the war talk hasn't stopped.
late.criticalFailure: An ambassador had been humiliated in public, and was humiliated again. The war talk has turned to war preparations.

early.criticalSuccess: A fishing boat hadn't come home from the lake. Searchers found it stuck on a sandbar with its crew cold but alive, and the village rang its bell all night.
early.success: A fishing boat hadn't come home from the lake. Searchers rowed out at dawn and found it drifting with a broken oar, and its crew came home safe.
early.failure: A fishing boat hadn't come home from the lake. It was found wrecked, and some of its crew were lost.
early.criticalFailure: A fishing boat hadn't come home from the lake, and it was never found. The village is in mourning.

middle.criticalSuccess: A cargo barge had broken up on the rapids, stranding its crew. They were rescued and the cargo salvaged too, and the bargemen toast the rescuers in every river tavern.
middle.success: A cargo barge had broken up on the rapids, stranding its crew on the rocks. They were roped across to the bank one by one and brought off safely.
middle.failure: A cargo barge had broken up on the rapids, stranding its crew. Most were rescued, but the cargo was lost.
middle.criticalFailure: A cargo barge had broken up on the rapids, stranding its crew, and the rescue failed. They were swept away.

late.criticalSuccess: A whole convoy had sunk in a storm with goods three nations were waiting on. The goods were salvaged, and all three nations are grateful for the realm's swift work.
late.success: A whole convoy had sunk in a storm with goods three nations were waiting on. Divers brought up much of the cargo, and the nations waiting on it were relieved.
late.failure: A whole convoy had sunk in a storm with goods three nations were waiting on. Some was saved, but they're angry about the rest.
late.criticalFailure: A whole convoy had sunk in a storm, and its goods were lost. Three nations are demanding the realm pay.

early.criticalSuccess: Kobolds had a captured trapper and wanted one of theirs back. The trade was made in a tense meeting at the edge of the woods, both sides left with new respect, and the kobolds even brought a gift.
early.success: Kobolds had a captured trapper and wanted one of theirs back. The two captives were traded at the edge of the woods, and both went home.
early.failure: Kobolds had a captured trapper and wanted one of theirs back. The trade went through, but the kobolds feel cheated.
early.criticalFailure: Kobolds had a captured trapper and wanted one of theirs back, and the exchange went wrong. The trapper was killed.

middle.criticalSuccess: A neighbor had offered to trade prisoners from the last skirmish. The exchange was handled with grace, the neighbor took it as a sign of good will, and peace feels closer.
middle.success: A neighbor had offered to trade prisoners from the last skirmish. The prisoners were exchanged at the border, and both sides are satisfied.
middle.failure: A neighbor had offered to trade prisoners from the last skirmish. They were exchanged, but some on both sides were left out.
middle.criticalFailure: A neighbor had offered to trade prisoners from the last skirmish, and the exchange fell apart. Fighting broke out again.

late.criticalSuccess: A powerful house had offered to swap fostered children with the court as a pledge of peace. The wards were exchanged with great ceremony, and the bond with the house is now unshakable.
late.success: A powerful house had offered to swap fostered children with the court as a pledge of peace. The wards were exchanged with proper ceremony, and the house counts the realm a friend.
late.failure: A powerful house had offered to swap fostered children as a pledge of peace. They were exchanged, but the house doesn't seem to trust the realm.
late.criticalFailure: A powerful house had offered to swap fostered children as a pledge of peace, and the exchange was bungled. The house has called off the pledge.

early.criticalSuccess: Fisherfolk wanted to hold boat races on the lake. Every fisher family for miles came, and the winning crew was carried through the village on their own boat.
early.success: Fisherfolk wanted to hold boat races on the lake. The races ran all afternoon with the whole shore cheering, and everyone had a fine day.
early.failure: Fisherfolk wanted to hold boat races on the lake, but rain kept the crowds away.
early.criticalFailure: Fisherfolk wanted to hold boat races on the lake, and a boat capsized mid-race. The day ended in a desperate rescue.

middle.criticalSuccess: River towns from three nations wanted to race on the realm's stretch of water. The regatta was a delight, the realm's own crew won the grand prize, and the river towns are still celebrating.
middle.success: River towns from three nations wanted to race on the realm's stretch of water. The regatta went off well, and the boats raced hard and fair.
middle.failure: River towns from three nations wanted to race on the realm's water, but the regatta was poorly run, and many boats didn't finish.
middle.criticalFailure: River towns from three nations raced on the realm's water, and the regatta ended in a brawl between crews. The nations are blaming each other.

late.criticalSuccess: Rulers along the river had proposed a gathering on the realm's shore, with everyone watching. It was a triumph of diplomacy and feasting, and the realm is now the river's leading power.
late.success: Rulers along the river had proposed a gathering on the realm's shore, with everyone watching. The gathering was well hosted, and the river kings went home on good terms.
late.failure: Rulers along the river had proposed a gathering on the realm's shore. It was held, but the river kings left unimpressed.
late.criticalFailure: Rulers along the river had gathered on the realm's shore, and the gathering ended in insults. They went home as enemies.

early.criticalSuccess: Merchants had been finding light coins in their tills. They were traced to a tinker shaving silver off good coin, he was caught with a bag of shavings, and the merchants got their losses back.
early.success: Merchants had been finding light coins in their tills. The coins were traced to a tinker shaving silver off good coin, he was caught, and the tills are honest again.
early.failure: Merchants had been finding light coins in their tills. The bad coins were pulled, but nobody found who made them, and merchants weigh every coin now.
early.criticalFailure: Merchants had been finding light coins in their tills, and nobody stopped it. Now they refuse any coin they don't know, and market days are shouting matches over the scales.

middle.criticalSuccess: Somebody was minting fake coin good enough to fool the moneychangers. The hidden mint was found in a cellar, and its master forger was set to work making the realm's coin harder to fake.
middle.success: Somebody was minting fake coin good enough to fool the moneychangers. The hidden mint was found and smashed, and the fakes are slowly leaving the markets.
middle.failure: Somebody was minting fake coin good enough to fool the moneychangers. The ring lost its mint but not its members, and a trickle of fakes goes on.
middle.criticalFailure: Somebody was minting fake coin, and the raid hit the wrong house. The real ring has flooded the markets with fakes in revenge.

late.criticalSuccess: False coin was everywhere, and folks had stopped trusting the realm's money. The flood was stopped at its source, new coin with clever marks was struck, and trust in the realm's money is stronger than ever.
late.success: False coin was everywhere, and folks had stopped trusting the realm's money. It was traced to its source and stopped, and trust in the coin is slowly coming back.
late.failure: False coin was everywhere, and folks had stopped trusting the realm's money. It was slowed but not stopped, and many still barter instead.
late.criticalFailure: False coin was everywhere, and it wrecked trust in the realm's money. Trade has collapsed into barter.

early.criticalSuccess: A blacksmith wanted to set up a forge if the crown helped with the first year's iron. The iron came, her forge rang from the first week, and a wheelwright and a cooper have settled beside her.
early.success: A blacksmith wanted to set up a forge if the crown helped with the first year's iron. The iron arrived on time, and her forge is ringing.
early.failure: A blacksmith wanted to set up a forge with the crown's help. The iron came late, and her first year was lean.
early.criticalFailure: A blacksmith wanted to set up a forge with the crown's help, and the iron never came. She packed up her anvil and left in disgust.

middle.criticalSuccess: Weavers wanted to build a hall and work together. The hall went up, and the cloth they make together sells in every market of the region.
middle.success: Weavers wanted to build a hall and work together. The hall was raised, and the weavers are working side by side under one roof.
middle.failure: Weavers wanted to build a hall and work together. It was built, but they keep quarrelling over the best looms.
middle.criticalFailure: Weavers wanted to build a hall and work together, and it burned before it opened. They've gone their separate ways.

late.criticalSuccess: Investors had proposed great workshops that could make the realm rich, or make a mess. They were built with care, they've made the realm rich, and their goods are prized across the Inner Sea.
late.success: Investors proposed great workshops that could make the realm rich, or make a mess. The workshops were built and well run, and they're turning a profit.
late.failure: Investors had proposed great workshops for the realm. They were built, but they're a mess of waste and quarrels.
late.criticalFailure: Investors had proposed great workshops for the realm, and they failed. The investors' money was lost, and the realm's with it.

early.criticalSuccess: The only salt seller in the village had tripled his prices. A rival was brought in from the next valley, he dropped his prices by morning, and the village salted its winter meat cheaply.
early.success: The only salt seller in the village had tripled his prices. He was talked into fair ones, and the village can afford to salt its meat again.
early.failure: The only salt seller in the village had tripled his prices. He dropped them a little, but not enough.
early.criticalFailure: The only salt seller in the village had tripled his prices, then raised them again. The village's winter stores are in danger.

middle.criticalSuccess: Merchants were hoarding grain to drive the price up before winter. The hoards were found and sold at a fair price, and the town ate well all winter.
middle.success: Merchants were hoarding grain to drive up the price before winter. They were made to open their stores and sell at fair prices.
middle.failure: Merchants were hoarding grain to drive the price up. Some hoards were found, but prices are still high.
middle.criticalFailure: Merchants were hoarding grain to drive the price up, and they got away with it. The town went hungry.

late.criticalSuccess: The big merchant houses had fixed prices across the realm, and folks were going hungry. The cartel was broken, prices are fair again, and folks bless the crown at every market.
late.success: The big merchant houses had fixed prices across the realm, and folks were going hungry. The cartel was broken up, and prices are coming down.
late.failure: The big merchant houses had fixed prices across the realm. The cartel was weakened, but prices are still high.
late.criticalFailure: The big merchant houses had fixed prices across the realm, and the cartel is stronger than ever. Folks are starving.

early.criticalSuccess: The village carpenters wanted to form a guild and set fair wages. The guild was formed with fair wages and good apprenticeships, and the village's buildings have never been better made.
early.success: The village carpenters wanted to form a guild and set fair wages. The guild was formed with fair wages agreed, and the carpenters toasted it at the inn.
early.failure: The village carpenters wanted to form a guild. It was formed, but they're quarrelling over the wages.
early.criticalFailure: The village carpenters wanted to form a guild, and it fell apart. They're undercutting each other.

middle.criticalSuccess: Craft guilds had asked for royal charters and the rights that come with them. They got their charters, their work has raised the realm's standards, and merchants trust the realm's goods.
middle.success: Craft guilds had asked for royal charters and the rights that come with them. The charters were granted, and the guilds are settling into their new standing.
middle.failure: Craft guilds had asked for royal charters. They got them, but they're squabbling over the rights.
middle.criticalFailure: Craft guilds had asked for royal charters and were refused. They're working against the crown.

late.criticalSuccess: Every guild in the realm wanted a seat on a council of trade. The council was formed, the guilds work together for the realm's good, and trade is booming.
late.success: Every guild in the realm wanted a seat on a council of trade. The council was formed, and the guilds have a voice in the realm's trade.
late.failure: Every guild in the realm wanted a seat on a council of trade. It was formed, but it's mostly bickering.
late.criticalFailure: Every guild in the realm wanted a seat on a council of trade, and the council turned against the crown. The guilds are on strike.

early.criticalSuccess: A whole village swore its tithes got lost on the road. They were found hidden in the miller's loft, and the village paid up with interest and an embarrassed apology.
early.success: A whole village swore its tithes had got lost on the road. The tithes turned up in the miller's loft, and the village paid.
early.failure: A whole village swore its tithes got lost on the road. Some were found, but the rest are still 'lost.'
early.criticalFailure: A whole village swore its tithes got lost on the road, and they were never found. Other villages are starting to lose theirs too.

middle.criticalSuccess: A merchant house had been keeping two sets of books. The hidden ledgers were found, the house paid back every coin it owed, and other merchants are suddenly paying promptly.
middle.success: A merchant house had been keeping two sets of books. The hidden ledgers were found, and the house paid what it owed.
middle.failure: A merchant house had been keeping two sets of books. The ledgers were found, but it paid only part of what it owed.
middle.criticalFailure: A merchant house had been keeping two sets of books, and the ledgers vanished before they could be seized. The house is laughing.

late.criticalSuccess: A province was refusing to pay, with good reasons and bad tempers. It got a fair hearing and lower taxes, and it has become loyal and prosperous.
late.success: A province was refusing to pay its taxes, with good reasons and bad tempers. Its complaints were heard, the revolt was settled, and the province is paying again.
late.failure: A province was refusing to pay its taxes. The revolt was settled, but the province is still angry.
late.criticalFailure: A province was refusing to pay its taxes, and the revolt spread to other provinces.

early.criticalSuccess: A small dig had collapsed with two miners trapped. Rescuers dug through the night and pulled both out alive and grinning, and the village threw them a feast that week.
early.success: A small dig had collapsed, trapping two miners. Rescuers dug through the night, and both were pulled out alive.
early.failure: A small dig had collapsed with two miners trapped. One was saved, but the other was lost.
early.criticalFailure: A small dig had collapsed with two miners trapped, and both were lost. The dig was abandoned.

middle.criticalSuccess: The mine's lower shafts had flooded, and work had stopped. They were pumped dry, a new seam was found in the process, and the mine is richer than ever.
middle.success: The mine's lower shafts had flooded, and work had stopped. Pumps were brought in and the shafts drained, and work has started again.
middle.failure: The mine's lower shafts had flooded, and work had stopped. They were partly drained, but work is slow.
middle.criticalFailure: The mine's lower shafts had flooded, and they flooded further. The mine was abandoned.

late.criticalSuccess: A whole mine had caved in, and the workers who got out wouldn't go back. It was reopened with new supports, they went back proudly, and it's the safest mine in the realm.
late.success: A whole mine had caved in, and the workers who got out wouldn't go back. New timbers were set and the shafts made safe, and the workers returned.
late.failure: A whole mine had caved in. It was reopened, but many workers refuse to go back.
late.criticalFailure: A whole mine had caved in, and it was lost. The workers have left the realm.

early.criticalSuccess: A peddler wanted to sell here every month if the road was safe. The road was made safe, and he comes as promised, bringing news and goods the village had only heard of.
early.success: A peddler wanted to sell here every month if the road was safe. Patrols kept the road clear, and the peddler comes every month.
early.failure: A peddler wanted to sell here every month if the road was safe. He came, but the road wasn't, and he's not sure he'll be back.
early.criticalFailure: A peddler wanted to sell here every month if the road was safe, and he was robbed on it. He swears he'll never return.

middle.criticalSuccess: A caravan master had offered to make the capital a regular stop. His wagons now roll in every season, and the markets are bursting with goods from far away.
middle.success: A caravan master had offered to make the capital a regular stop. The capital is on his route now, and his wagons roll in every season.
middle.failure: A caravan master had offered to make the capital a regular stop, but he comes rarely.
middle.criticalFailure: A caravan master had offered to make the capital a regular stop, and he was cheated there. He's crossed it off his route.

late.criticalSuccess: Great merchant houses had proposed a trade road through the realm. It was built, the realm has become a hub of trade, and the coffers are full.
late.success: Great merchant houses had proposed a trade road through the realm. The road was built, and the merchants' wagons are using it.
late.failure: Great merchant houses had proposed a trade road through the realm. It was built, but it's not as busy as hoped.
late.criticalFailure: Great merchant houses had proposed a trade road through the realm, and in the end they routed it around the realm instead.

early.criticalSuccess: A moneylender was calling in debts all at once, and families were losing their homes. He was persuaded to give them more time, the crown helped them pay, and no one lost their home.
early.success: A moneylender was calling in debts all at once, and families were losing their homes. He was talked into easing his demands, and the families have time to pay.
early.failure: A moneylender was calling in debts all at once. He eased up a little, but some families lost their homes.
early.criticalFailure: A moneylender was calling in debts all at once, and he took the homes. Families are on the road.

middle.criticalSuccess: A Brevic bank claimed the realm owed it for loans taken before the founding. The claim was shown to be a fraud, and the bank withdrew it with an apology.
middle.success: A Brevic bank claimed the realm owed it for loans taken before the founding. The claim was settled for a fair sum, and the matter is closed.
middle.failure: A Brevic bank claimed the realm owed it for old loans. It was settled, but for more than the realm wanted to pay.
middle.criticalFailure: A Brevic bank claimed the realm owed it for old loans, and it pressed the claim and won. The realm owes a great deal.

late.criticalSuccess: Foreign creditors had seized the realm's merchants' goods downriver. A clever deal paid them off, and the goods came back with interest.
late.success: Foreign creditors had seized the realm's merchants' goods downriver. They were paid, and the goods were released.
late.failure: Foreign creditors had seized the realm's merchants' goods downriver. They were paid, but only some of the goods came back.
late.criticalFailure: Foreign creditors had seized the realm's merchants' goods downriver, and they kept them. They're demanding more.

early.criticalSuccess: Trappers wanted the forest trails marked so folks would stop getting lost. They walked every trail with paint pots and hatchets, and not one traveler has got lost since.
early.success: Trappers wanted the forest trails marked so folks would stop getting lost. The trails were blazed with bright paint, and folks find their way through the woods now.
early.failure: Trappers wanted the forest trails marked, but the blazes went up patchy and confusing. A peddler got lost following them last week.
early.criticalFailure: Trappers wanted the forest trails marked, and someone painted the wrong trails. Two families followed them deep into the woods before searchers found them.

middle.criticalSuccess: A surveyor had offered to map the land between the settlements. He mapped every road and track, found a shortcut that cut a day off the trade route, and merchants call it the crown's road.
middle.success: A surveyor had offered to map the land between the settlements properly. The map was finished, and travel between the settlements is easier for it.
middle.failure: A surveyor had offered to map the land between the settlements. The map was finished, but its mistakes send carts down tracks that peter out.
middle.criticalFailure: A surveyor had offered to map the land between the settlements, and he wandered into a bandit camp. He was held for ransom, and the map was never finished.

late.criticalSuccess: Cartographers had proposed mapping the whole realm, every hill and ford. The great survey's maps are so fine that foreign lords pay to copy them.
late.success: Cartographers had proposed mapping the whole realm, every hill and ford. The great survey was finished, and its maps hang in every town hall.
late.failure: Cartographers had proposed mapping the whole realm. It was finished in a hurry, and its maps have gaps.
late.criticalFailure: Cartographers had proposed mapping the whole realm, and the survey party was lost in the wilds. The maps they sent back are wrong in dangerous ways.

early.criticalSuccess: Two hunters had gone into the Narlmarches three days earlier and hadn't come out. Searchers found them up a tree with a bear asleep at its foot, and they came home hungry, sheepish and very much alive.
early.success: Two hunters had gone into the Narlmarches three days earlier and hadn't come out. Searchers found them by their smoke, cold and hungry but safe, and brought them home.
early.failure: Two hunters had gone into the Narlmarches and hadn't come out. One was found wandering at the forest's edge; the other is still missing.
early.criticalFailure: Two hunters had gone into the Narlmarches and hadn't come out, and the search party came back without them and short one searcher.

middle.criticalSuccess: A ranger patrol had missed its check-in, and its trail went cold at a river. It was picked up downstream, and the rangers were found holding off a band of trolls. They were rescued, and the trolls driven off.
middle.success: A ranger patrol had missed its check-in, and its trail went cold at a river. Trackers picked it up again downstream, and the patrol was found battered but alive.
middle.failure: A ranger patrol had missed its check-in. Some of the rangers were found, but others are still lost.
middle.criticalFailure: A ranger patrol had missed its check-in, and it was never found. The rangers refuse to patrol that stretch of river.

late.criticalSuccess: A whole village's hunting party had vanished, and something was leaving signs at the treeline. The signs were read as a forest spirit's warning, a bargain was struck, and the party came home safe.
late.success: A whole village's hunting party had vanished, and something was leaving signs at the treeline. The party was found and brought home, and the signs have stopped.
late.failure: A whole village's hunting party had vanished. Some were found, but the signs at the treeline keep appearing.
late.criticalFailure: A whole village's hunting party had vanished, and it was never found. The signs have started appearing inside the village.

early.criticalSuccess: Someone was setting snares in the woods the crown keeps for itself. The poacher turned out to be a widow feeding her children, she was given work as a gamekeeper, and the snares disappeared.
early.success: Someone was setting snares in the woods the crown keeps for itself. The poacher was caught checking his snares, and the snaring stopped.
early.failure: Someone was setting snares in the crown's woods. The snares were pulled, but new ones keep appearing.
early.criticalFailure: Someone was setting snares in the crown's woods, and they caught a royal stag and sold it at market. Folks are laughing at the crown.

middle.criticalSuccess: A gang was taking deer by the cartload and selling the meat across the border. They were caught with a full cart, the meat went to the hungry, and the ringleader now works for the crown.
middle.success: A gang was taking deer by the cartload and selling the meat across the border. The gang was caught at the border with a full cart and broken up, and the deer are safe again.
middle.failure: A gang was taking deer by the cartload. It was broken up, but some of its members have started again.
middle.criticalFailure: A gang was taking deer by the cartload, and it fought off the wardens and escaped across the border.

late.criticalSuccess: Foreign nobles were holding hunts on the realm's land without asking. They were invited to a royal hunt instead and taught some manners, and they left as friends who paid well for the privilege.
late.success: Foreign nobles were holding hunts on the realm's land without asking. They were told politely but firmly to ask first, and the uninvited hunts stopped.
late.failure: Foreign nobles were holding hunts on the realm's land without asking. They were warned, but some still do.
late.criticalFailure: Foreign nobles were holding hunts on the realm's land without asking, and they laughed off the warning. Their hunts have grown bolder.

early.criticalSuccess: The mushrooms were in, and the foragers said it was the best year in memory. Baskets of them came in, and the mushroom feast drew guests from three valleys.
early.success: The mushrooms were in, and the foragers said it was the best year in memory. Baskets of them were gathered and sold well at market.
early.failure: The mushrooms were in, and it was the best year in memory, but much of the harvest rotted before it could be sold.
early.criticalFailure: The mushrooms were in, and a forager mistook a deadly one for a good one. Half the village fell sick.

middle.criticalSuccess: Wild hives in the hills could supply the whole realm with honey and wax. A clever beekeeper tamed them, and the realm's honey and wax sell across the region.
middle.success: Wild hives in the hills could supply the whole realm with honey and wax. They were harvested carefully, and the honey and wax sold well.
middle.failure: Wild hives in the hills could supply honey and wax. They were harvested, but the bees swarmed and stung several folk.
middle.criticalFailure: Wild hives in the hills could supply honey and wax, and careless harvesters destroyed them. The bees are gone.

late.criticalSuccess: A rare tree had bloomed across the forest, its fruit worth a fortune. The fruit was harvested with care and fetched a fortune, and the trees were tended so they'll bloom again.
late.success: A rare tree had come into bloom across the forest, and its fruit was worth a fortune. The fruit was gathered and sold, and the realm made a good price on it.
late.failure: A rare tree had bloomed across the forest. Some fruit was gathered, but much of it fell and rotted.
late.criticalFailure: A rare tree had bloomed across the forest, and greedy harvesters stripped it bare and damaged the trees. They may never bloom again.

early.criticalSuccess: Herders had found tracks by the pond that nobody could name. They led to a giant heron's nest, harmless, and the village now counts the bird as a lucky omen.
early.success: Herders had found tracks by the pond that nobody could name. A hunter followed them to a harmless giant heron, and the herders laughed at themselves.
early.failure: Herders had found tracks by the pond that nobody could name. They're still a mystery, and the herders are nervous.
early.criticalFailure: Herders had found tracks by the pond that nobody could name, and they led to something that killed a herder's dog.

middle.criticalSuccess: Livestock kept going missing near the hills, and the tracks were getting bigger. The creature was tracked to its lair and slain, and its hide hangs in the town hall.
middle.success: Livestock kept going missing near the hills, and the tracks were getting bigger. Hunters drove the creature off into the high hills, and the herds are safe.
middle.failure: Livestock kept going missing near the hills. The creature was wounded, but it's still taking animals.
middle.criticalFailure: Livestock kept going missing near the hills, and the creature killed the hunters sent after it.

late.criticalSuccess: A trail of broken trees ran across three provinces, heading for a town. The beast was turned aside and slain in the forest, and the realm's hunters are famous for it.
late.success: A trail of broken trees ran across three provinces, heading for a town. The beast was turned aside with fire and noise before it reached the town.
late.failure: A trail of broken trees ran across three provinces, heading for a town. The beast was turned aside, but it's still loose.
late.criticalFailure: A trail of broken trees ran across three provinces, and the beast reached the town. The damage is terrible.

early.criticalSuccess: A shepherd had found carved stones in a meadow. They proved to be part of an ancient shrine, scholars came to study them, and the meadow is now a place of wonder.
early.success: A shepherd had found carved stones in a meadow. Scholars came to study them and found they were from an old shrine.
early.failure: A shepherd had found carved stones in a meadow. They were studied, but no one can read them.
early.criticalFailure: A shepherd had found carved stones in a meadow, and treasure hunters carted them off before anyone could study them.

middle.criticalSuccess: Explorers had found a ruin nobody knew about, half buried in the hills. It was explored, treasures and lore came out safely, and the scholars are delighted.
middle.success: Explorers had found a ruin nobody knew about, half buried in the hills. It was explored room by room, and some treasures were brought out.
middle.failure: Explorers had found a ruin half buried in the hills. It was explored, but little of value was found.
middle.criticalFailure: Explorers had found a ruin half buried in the hills, and they woke something in it. It's still angry.

late.criticalSuccess: An expedition swore it had found the edge of a lost city past the frontier. It was explored and its secrets brought home, and the realm's scholars and treasury are both richer.
late.success: An expedition swore it had found the edge of a lost city past the frontier. It was explored, and wagons of its riches were brought home.
late.failure: An expedition swore it had found a lost city past the frontier. It found the city, but couldn't bring much back.
late.criticalFailure: An expedition went looking for a lost city past the frontier, and it vanished without a trace.

early.criticalSuccess: There was smoke on the ridge, and the wind was turning toward the village. Everyone turned out with buckets and shovels, a firebreak was cut just in time, and not a roof was singed.
early.success: There was smoke on the ridge, and the wind was turning toward the village. A firebreak was cut and the fire beaten back before it reached the houses.
early.failure: There was smoke on the ridge, and the wind was turning toward the village. The fire was turned, but it took the woodlot and two sheds.
early.criticalFailure: There was smoke on the ridge, and the wind carried the fire into the village before anyone could stop it. Several homes burned.

middle.criticalSuccess: A wildfire was burning through the woods and the farms beyond them. Firebreaks and river water stopped it before it reached a single farm, and the firefighters were feasted as heroes.
middle.success: A wildfire was burning through the woods and the farms beyond them. Firebreaks stopped it at the edge of the woods, and the farms were saved.
middle.failure: A wildfire was burning through the woods toward the farms. It was stopped, but not before it took some of them.
middle.criticalFailure: A wildfire was burning through the woods, and it swept through the farms beyond. Families have lost everything.

late.criticalSuccess: A great forest was on fire, and the smoke could be seen from the capital. Every hand in the realm fought it until it was out, and the forest is already greening again.
late.success: A great forest was on fire, and the smoke could be seen from the capital. After weeks of work it was finally put out, and the smoke has cleared.
late.failure: A great forest was on fire, and the smoke could be seen from the capital. It was put out, but a great stretch of forest is gone.
late.criticalFailure: A great forest was on fire, and it burned for weeks. The forest and the villages around it are ash.

early.criticalSuccess: Young folks wanted to scout the land past the border. They came back with tales of a good valley and a clear spring, and settlers are already talking of moving there.
early.success: Young folks wanted to scout the land past the border. They went over the hill and came back with useful news of the land beyond.
early.failure: Young folks wanted to scout the land past the border. They went, but came back with little to report.
early.criticalFailure: Young folks wanted to scout the land past the border, and one didn't come back. The village blames the crown for letting them go.

middle.criticalSuccess: Veteran rangers had offered to patrol the frontier if the crown paid them. They do, and they've already caught two bands of raiders before they could strike.
middle.success: Veteran rangers had offered to patrol the frontier if the crown paid them. They were hired, and they ride the frontier every day.
middle.failure: Veteran rangers had offered to patrol the frontier. They were hired, but they're too few to watch it all.
middle.criticalFailure: Veteran rangers had offered to patrol the frontier, and they spent the crown's pay drinking.

late.criticalSuccess: Rangers had proposed a proper order of wardens to watch the realm's edges. It was founded, and not a raider has crossed the border unseen since.
late.success: Rangers had proposed a proper order of wardens to watch the whole realm's edges. The order was founded, and its wardens watch the borders.
late.failure: Rangers had proposed a proper order of wardens. It was founded, but it's poorly organized.
late.criticalFailure: Rangers had proposed a proper order of wardens, and it fell apart over who would lead it.

early.criticalSuccess: The village smith had asked for a strip of crown land to build a bigger shop. He got it, the new shop went up fast, and his work is now known across the province.
early.success: The village smith had asked for a strip of crown land to build a bigger shop. He got a good strip by the road, and the new shop is going up.
early.failure: The village smith had asked for a strip of crown land. He got a poor, boggy strip, and his new shop is slow to rise.
early.criticalFailure: The village smith had asked for a strip of crown land, and it was given to someone else. He packed up his anvil and left the village.

middle.criticalSuccess: Captains and clerks who had served well asked for land grants as reward. They were given generous holdings, and their loyalty to the crown is now unshakeable.
middle.success: Captains and clerks who had served well asked for land grants as reward. Each was given a modest holding with a deed sealed by the crown, and they're content.
middle.failure: Captains and clerks who had served well asked for land grants. They got them, but some feel they got less than they deserved.
middle.criticalFailure: Captains and clerks who had served well asked for land grants, and the grants were bungled. Some loyal servants got nothing, and they're angry.

late.criticalSuccess: Loyal houses had asked to be raised to baronies with lands of their own. They were, and they've become pillars of the realm whose lands are flourishing.
late.success: Loyal houses had asked to be raised to baronies with lands of their own. The new baronies were made in a proper ceremony, and the houses are pleased.
late.failure: Loyal houses had asked to be raised to baronies. They were, but the lesser houses passed over are jealous.
late.criticalFailure: Loyal houses had been raised to baronies with lands of their own, and the new barons have started acting like kings.

early.criticalSuccess: A new rule about keeping pigs in town had folks furious. It was rewritten with the townsfolk's help, now everyone agrees it's sensible, and the pigs seem happy too.
early.success: A new rule about keeping pigs in town had folks furious. It was changed so pigs can stay in yards but not the street, and the town has calmed down.
early.failure: A new rule about keeping pigs in town had folks furious. It stands as written, and the grumbling goes on.
early.criticalFailure: A new rule about keeping pigs in town had folks furious, and it was enforced harshly. There was nearly a riot in the market.

middle.criticalSuccess: A curfew meant to stop thieves had started fights in the streets instead. It was lifted and replaced with better watches, the thieves were caught anyway, and the streets are peaceful.
middle.success: A curfew meant to stop thieves had started fights in the streets instead. It was eased to the small hours only, and the fights have stopped.
middle.failure: A curfew meant to stop thieves had started fights in the streets. It was kept, and the fights go on every night.
middle.criticalFailure: A curfew meant to stop thieves had started fights in the streets, and it was enforced with clubs. The fights have become riots.

late.criticalSuccess: A royal edict had whole provinces refusing to obey. It was withdrawn with grace, and the crown's willingness to listen has won the provinces back.
late.success: A royal edict had whole provinces refusing to obey. It was amended to meet their worst complaints, and the provinces have begun to comply.
late.failure: A royal edict had whole provinces refusing to obey. It was softened, but the provinces are still defiant.
late.criticalFailure: A royal edict had whole provinces refusing to obey, and the crown tried to force it. They're in open revolt.

early.criticalSuccess: The reeve's seal had gone missing, and forged permits were turning up. It was found in a light-fingered clerk's pocket, every forged permit was voided, and the reeve has a new lockbox.
early.success: The reeve's seal had gone missing, and forged permits were turning up. The seal was found under a loose floorboard, and the forged permits were cancelled.
early.failure: The reeve's seal had gone missing, and forged permits were turning up. A new seal was made, but the forged permits keep appearing.
early.criticalFailure: The reeve's seal had gone missing, and it was never found. Forged permits are everywhere.

middle.criticalSuccess: Writs with the council's seal were ordering things the council never ordered. The forger was caught, every false writ was undone, and the council has a new seal and stricter rules.
middle.success: Writs with the council's seal were ordering things the council never ordered. They were stopped and the seal was changed, and the council's orders can be trusted again.
middle.failure: Writs with the council's seal were ordering things the council never ordered. The forger was caught, but some false writs were obeyed first.
middle.criticalFailure: Writs with the council's seal were ordering things the council never ordered, and they caused chaos. Now its real orders are being ignored.

late.criticalSuccess: The crown's own signet was gone, and someone was using it. It was recovered and the thief unmasked as a foreign agent, and the realm's enemies are thoroughly embarrassed.
late.success: The crown's own signet was gone, and someone was using it. It was recovered, and every false order it had sealed was undone.
late.failure: The crown's own signet was gone, and someone was using it. It was recovered, but not before it did real damage.
late.criticalFailure: The crown's own signet was gone, and its thief is still at large. Nobody knows which royal orders to trust.

early.criticalSuccess: New settlers wanted to swear loyalty to the realm properly, with a leader present. They swore with their hands on the realm's banner, and they've become its most loyal citizens.
early.success: New settlers wanted to swear loyalty to the realm properly, with a leader present. A leader came and heard each oath in turn, and it meant a great deal to the settlers.
early.failure: New settlers wanted to swear loyalty to the realm properly, but the swearing in was rushed, and they felt it was hollow.
early.criticalFailure: New settlers wanted to swear loyalty to the realm properly, and the leader who came was late and rude. They wonder why they bothered.

middle.criticalSuccess: Local lords had offered to swear fealty in public if the crown would host it. The ceremony was grand, the people cheered as their lords knelt, and the bond is stronger than ever.
middle.success: Local lords had offered to swear fealty in public if the crown would host it. The crown hosted a fine ceremony, and the oaths were sworn before the people.
middle.failure: Local lords had offered to swear fealty in public. The oaths were sworn, but some lords did it with poor grace.
middle.criticalFailure: Local lords had offered to swear fealty in public, and some refused at the last moment. The ceremony became a scandal.

late.criticalSuccess: Every lord and mayor in the realm could renew their oaths in one great ceremony. They all came and knelt together in the capital's square, and the realm has never been so united.
late.success: Every lord and mayor in the realm could renew their oaths in one great ceremony. They came, the great oath was taken, and the realm's loyalties are renewed.
late.failure: Every lord and mayor in the realm was called to renew their oaths, but many stayed away. The great oath felt half empty.
late.criticalFailure: Every lord and mayor in the realm was called to renew their oaths, and several walked out in the middle. The realm is split.

early.criticalSuccess: Three children had turned up at the village alone, and nobody knew whose they were. They were taken in by good families, one turned out to be a lost heir, and the village loves to tell the story.
early.success: Three children had turned up at the village alone, and nobody knew whose they were. Families took them in, and they're settling into village life.
early.failure: Three children had turned up at the village alone. They were taken in, but nobody is happy about the extra mouths.
early.criticalFailure: Three children had turned up at the village alone, and they ran off again before anyone took them in. Nobody knows where they went.

middle.criticalSuccess: Orphans were sleeping in the town's alleys, and the temples were full. A new orphanage was built, the children were given homes and schooling, and the town is proud of it.
middle.success: Orphans were sleeping in the town's alleys, and the temples were full. A house was found and staffed for them, and the alleys are empty.
middle.failure: Orphans were sleeping in the town's alleys. Some were given shelter, but many still sleep rough.
middle.criticalFailure: Orphans were sleeping in the town's alleys, and they were driven out of town. Folks are ashamed.

late.criticalSuccess: War and sickness had left hundreds of children with no one. They were given homes across the realm, and they've grown up to be its most loyal citizens.
late.success: War and sickness had left hundreds of children with no one. Homes and temples across the realm took them in, and each child has a roof and someone to look after them.
late.failure: War and sickness had left hundreds of children with no one. Some were given homes, but many still wander.
late.criticalFailure: War and sickness had left hundreds of children with no one, and they were neglected. Many have turned to crime.

early.criticalSuccess: A woodcarver had offered to carve a sign for the village hall. It's a masterpiece, and the hall is now the prettiest in the province.
early.success: A woodcarver had offered to carve a sign for the village hall. The sign went up over the door, and it's a fine piece of work.
early.failure: A woodcarver had offered to carve a sign for the village hall. He carved it well enough, but it went up crooked, and nobody can bring themselves to tell him.
early.criticalFailure: A woodcarver had offered to carve a sign for the village hall, and he hid a rude joke in it. The village is embarrassed.

middle.criticalSuccess: A sculptor wanted to build a fountain in the town square. It's a wonder, and the square is now the most beautiful in the realm.
middle.success: A sculptor wanted to build a fountain in the town square. The fountain was finished by midsummer, and it's a handsome thing.
middle.failure: A sculptor wanted to build a fountain in the town square. It was built, but it barely trickles.
middle.criticalFailure: A sculptor wanted to build a fountain in the town square, and it cracked and flooded the square.

late.criticalSuccess: A master sculptor proposed a great statue of the founders that could be seen for miles. The colossus was raised, and the realm's name is spoken with awe.
late.success: A master sculptor proposed a great statue of the founders that could be seen for miles. The colossus was raised on the hill above the capital, and travelers stop on the road to stare at it.
late.failure: A master sculptor proposed a great statue of the founders. It was raised, but it's ugly.
late.criticalFailure: A master sculptor proposed a great statue of the founders, and it collapsed during the raising. People were killed.

early.criticalSuccess: The village shrine wanted to honor its saint with a feast. It was a joy, and the shrine has never been so full.
early.success: The village shrine wanted to honor its saint with a feast. The feast was held with songs and good bread, and the shrine was full.
early.failure: The village shrine wanted to honor its saint with a feast, but it was small and quiet.
early.criticalFailure: The village shrine wanted to honor its saint with a feast, and a sudden storm ruined it. Folks think the saint is angry.

middle.criticalSuccess: Pilgrims wanted a road and inns to reach a holy site in the realm. They were built, pilgrims are pouring in, and the realm feels blessed.
middle.success: Pilgrims wanted a road and inns to reach a holy site in the realm. The road was cleared and three inns built along it, and pilgrims have started making the journey.
middle.failure: Pilgrims wanted a road and inns to reach a holy site. The road was built, but the inns are poor, and few pilgrims come.
middle.criticalFailure: Pilgrims wanted a road and inns to reach a holy site, and bandits found the road first. Pilgrims were robbed.

late.criticalSuccess: A great temple had offered to lend a sacred relic for a year, if it was treated right. It was honored all year, and the temple was so pleased that it gave the realm a lasting blessing.
late.success: A great temple had offered to lend a sacred relic for a year, if it was treated right. It was honored and guarded all year, and the temple is pleased.
late.failure: A great temple had offered to lend a sacred relic for a year, but it was treated poorly, and the temple is displeased.
late.criticalFailure: A great temple had lent a sacred relic for a year, and it was stolen. The temple has cursed the realm.

early.criticalSuccess: A catchy and very rude song about the leaders was going round. It was answered with an even funnier song about the songwriter, and the village laughed along with the leaders.
early.success: A catchy and very rude song about the leaders was going round. The leaders laughed along with it in public, and it's lost its sting.
early.failure: A catchy and very rude song about the leaders was going round. It's still going round, and it's getting ruder.
early.criticalFailure: A catchy and very rude song about the leaders was going round, and the leaders tried to ban it. Now everyone sings it louder.

middle.criticalSuccess: A satirist's plays were making the court look foolish, and the crowds loved them. The satirist was invited to court and charmed into writing a play that made it look good, and the crowds love that one too.
middle.success: A satirist's plays were making the court look foolish, and the crowds loved them. The court laughed them off, and they've lost their bite.
middle.failure: A satirist's plays were making the court look foolish, and nothing done about it worked. The crowds keep laughing, and the court keeps looking foolish.
middle.criticalFailure: A satirist's plays were making the court look foolish, and the satirist was arrested. The crowds rioted.

late.criticalSuccess: A song that sounded a lot like a call to revolt was spreading across the realm. It was answered by a song of loyalty that swept the realm, and the rebels are forgotten.
late.success: A song that sounded a lot like a call to revolt was spreading across the realm. Folks sang it, but nobody rose to it, and it faded away by midwinter.
late.failure: A song that sounded like a call to revolt was spreading across the realm. It's still sung in secret.
late.criticalFailure: A song that sounded like a call to revolt was spreading across the realm, and it started real riots.

early.criticalSuccess: A militia drill had gone wrong, and a farmhand took a spear through the leg. The wound was tended quickly and he walks without a limp, the drill leader was retrained, and the village trusts its militia more than ever.
early.success: A militia drill had gone wrong, and a farmhand took a spear through the leg. A healer was sent for, the wound was stitched, and his family was paid for the work he'll miss. The drills go on, with more care.
early.failure: A militia drill had gone wrong, and a farmhand took a spear through the leg. He'll limp for life, and the village whispers that the militia is careless.
early.criticalFailure: A militia drill had gone wrong, and a farmhand took a spear through the leg. The wound festered and he died, and the village has turned against the militia. Nobody will drill now.

middle.criticalSuccess: Two companies had brawled in the barracks over an insult, and their officers joined in. Fair punishments were handed out, then both companies were set to rebuild the barracks together, and they've come out of it the best of friends.
middle.success: Two companies had brawled in the barracks over an insult, and their officers joined in. The brawlers were punished fairly, the insult was apologized for in front of both companies, and they serve side by side again.
middle.failure: Two companies had brawled in the barracks over an insult. Punishments were handed out, but each company thinks it was the one wronged, and the grudge simmers.
middle.criticalFailure: Two companies had brawled in the barracks over an insult, and the punishments that followed were so uneven that one company mutinied. The barracks are split down the middle.

late.criticalSuccess: Troops on maneuvers had burned a village they mistook for an enemy camp. The army rebuilt it better than before, the officers were tried in public, and the families have forgiven. Folks across the realm admire the justice done.
late.success: Troops on maneuvers had burned a village they mistook for an enemy camp. The army paid to rebuild every house, and the officers who gave the order were stripped of rank in public.
late.failure: Troops on maneuvers had burned a village they mistook for an enemy camp. The villagers got some coin and an apology, but no one was punished, and the anger lingers.
late.criticalFailure: Troops on maneuvers had burned a village they mistook for an enemy camp, and the whole thing was hushed up. When the truth came out, folks across the realm were horrified.

early.criticalSuccess: An old palisade near the village could be patched up and used again. Fresh logs and a new gate made it sturdier than when it was first built, and the village sleeps soundly behind it.
early.success: An old palisade near the village could be patched up and used again. Fresh logs went in where the old ones had rotted and the gate was rehung, and the village has a wall to shelter behind if trouble comes.
early.failure: An old palisade near the village needed patching, but the timber ran out halfway. It's only half a wall now, and everyone knows which half.
early.criticalFailure: An old palisade near the village needed patching, but it was more rot than wood. It collapsed on the work crew, two were hurt, and the effort was abandoned.

middle.criticalSuccess: A keep from before the founding stood empty on a good hill. It was cleared, repaired and garrisoned, and now it's a proud stronghold watching over the whole valley.
middle.success: A keep from before the founding stood empty on a good hill. Masons and a small garrison were sent, the walls were patched and the gate rebuilt, and the hill belongs to the realm again.
middle.failure: A keep from before the founding stood empty on a good hill. Its walls were partly repaired, but it needs more stone and more soldiers than the realm can spare.
middle.criticalFailure: A keep from before the founding stood empty on a good hill, and something nasty was living in it. The work crew fled, and the keep's name is worse than before.

late.criticalSuccess: Engineers had proposed a chain of forts along the frontier. The forts went up on time and under budget, and enemies of the realm look at that line of stone and think twice.
late.success: Engineers had proposed a chain of forts along the frontier. It cost a small fortune in stone and labor, but the forts were finished, and the border is far safer for them.
late.failure: Engineers had proposed a chain of forts along the frontier, but the money ran short with only half of them finished. There are gaps an enemy could find.
late.criticalFailure: Engineers had proposed a chain of forts along the frontier, and the work became a swamp of graft and bad stone. Forts crumbled before they were even finished.

early.criticalSuccess: A few sellswords at the inn were looking for work guarding the roads. They were hired on fair terms, proved honest and hard-working, and the roads have never been safer.
early.success: A few sellswords at the inn were looking for work guarding the roads. They were hired for the season, rode the roads every day and chased off two bands of thieves, and they earn every coin of their pay.
early.failure: A few sellswords at the inn were looking for work guarding the roads. They took the coin and did as little as they could, and the roads are no safer.
early.criticalFailure: A few sellswords at the inn were hired to guard the roads. They robbed the very travelers they were meant to protect, then vanished with their pay.

middle.criticalSuccess: A mercenary company had offered its swords for the season. It signed on and fought like the realm's own, and its captain is talking about settling here for good.
middle.success: A mercenary company had offered its swords for the season. It served well, kept its drinking to the taverns, and parted on good terms with its pay in hand.
middle.failure: A mercenary company had offered its swords for the season. It served, but cost more than it was worth and drank the towns dry along the way.
middle.criticalFailure: A mercenary company had offered its swords for the season, and halfway through it turned on the realm. It had to be paid off to leave.

late.criticalSuccess: A famous mercenary general had offered an army for hire. A fair price was struck, and the army's mere presence has made the realm's enemies very nervous and kept the peace.
late.success: A famous mercenary general had offered an army for hire. The price was high, but the realm now has one of the best armies in the River Kingdoms at its call, and its neighbors know it.
late.failure: A famous mercenary general had offered an army for hire. The price was crushing, and it's not clear what the army has done to earn it.
late.criticalFailure: A famous mercenary general had offered an army for hire. He took the realm's coin and then sold his services to its rival.

early.criticalSuccess: A rumor that raiders were coming had the village barricading itself. The tale was traced to a drunk tinker and laughed out of town, and the barricade timber became a new market stall.
early.success: A rumor that raiders were coming had the village barricading itself. A rider was sent to every road to look, came back with nothing to report, and the villagers sheepishly took their barricades down.
early.failure: A rumor that raiders were coming had the village barricading itself, and it wouldn't take the barricades down. Travelers are turned away, and trade has dried up.
early.criticalFailure: A rumor that raiders were coming had the village barricading itself, and panicking villagers attacked a band of travelers they took for raiders. Someone is dead, and the panic has spread.

middle.criticalSuccess: A town was hoarding food and turning travelers away, sure it was about to be attacked. It was shown there was no threat, shared its stores with the hungry villages around it, and has become a model of good sense.
middle.success: A town was hoarding food and turning travelers away, sure it was about to be attacked. Patrols showed there was no army anywhere near, the town calmed down, and it opened its gates again.
middle.failure: A town was hoarding food and turning travelers away, sure an attack was coming. It opened its gates, but it's still hoarding, and prices are high and tempers short.
middle.criticalFailure: A town was hoarding food and turning travelers away, sure an attack was coming. The fever spread to the next town, and now two settlements are shut tight and accusing each other.

late.criticalSuccess: Half the realm believed an army was coming, and folks were fleeing toward the capital. The crown showed its people there was no army, the families went home in good spirits, and the rumor-mongers were found and shamed.
late.success: Half the realm believed an army was coming, and folks were fleeing toward the capital. Heralds rode out to every town to say there was no army, the panic died down, and most of the families went home.
late.failure: Half the realm believed an army was coming, and folks were fleeing toward the capital. The panic eased, but many families stayed packed and ready, not quite trusting the crown's word.
